- [bruinier-funke-2004](#reference-bruinier-funke-2004), §3, p. 10. Exactly the statement.

Direct prerequisites: [QM.3/harmonic-fourier-coefficient-ode](#QM-3-harmonic-fourier-coefficient-ode), [QM.3/upper-incomplete-gamma](#QM-3-upper-incomplete-gamma), [QM.3/nonholomorphic-fourier-basis-growing](#QM-3-nonholomorphic-fourier-basis-growing).

Construction or proof route:

1. |a(n; v)| ≤ sup_u |f(u + iv)| ≤ A e^{Cv} for v ≥ v₀.
2. For n < 0: the β-term Γ(1−k, 4π|n|v/h)e^{2π|n|v/h} = O(v^{−k}e^{−2π|n|v/h}) is bounded, so α_n e^{2π|n|v/h} = O(e^{Cv}) forces α_n = 0 when 2π|n|/h > C.
3. For n > 0: the β-term grows like ½W^{−k}e^{W} with W = 2πnv/h, while e^{−W} decays, so β_n = 0 when 2πn/h > C.

Acceptance checks:

- For f = 1/Δ (k = −12): α_n = 0 for n < −1; β_n = 0 for all n.

<a id="QM-3-xi-map"></a>

### ξ_k as a conjugate-linear map H_k(Γ) → M^!_{2−k}(Γ)

**Construction** (`QM.3/xi-map`). Let Γ ≤ GL₂(ℝ) be arithmetic with Γ.HasDetOne and k ∈ ℤ, k ≠ 1. For f ∈ H_k(Γ), ξ_k f (QM.3/xi-operator) is a weakly holomorphic modular form of weight 2 − k for Γ, and f ↦ ξ_k f is a conjugate-linear map ξ_k : H_k(Γ) → M^!_{2−k}(Γ) (Bruinier–Funke Prop. 3.2).

Hypotheses and conventions:

- Γ arithmetic and Γ.HasDetOne (e.g. the image of a finite-index subgroup of SL₂(ℤ)); k ∈ ℤ, k ≠ 1.
- Conjugate-linear: a σ-semilinear map for σ = complex conjugation (Mathlib's →ₗ⋆[ℂ]).

Source support:

- [bruinier-funke-2004](#reference-bruinier-funke-2004), Prop. 3.2 and proof, p. 10. The construction; the growth step follows BF's 'It is meromorphic at the cusp via the growth condition on f'.

Direct prerequisites: [QM.3/harmonic-maass-form](#QM-3-harmonic-maass-form), [QM.3/weakly-holomorphic-modular-form](#QM-3-weakly-holomorphic-modular-form), [QM.3/xi-holomorphic-iff-harmonic](#QM-3-xi-holomorphic-iff-harmonic), [QM.3/xi-slash-equivariance](#QM-3-xi-slash-equivariance), [QM.3/harmonic-fourier-coefficient-ode](#QM-3-harmonic-fourier-coefficient-ode), [QM.3/harmonic-coefficients-eventually-zero](#QM-3-harmonic-coefficients-eventually-zero), [QM.3/nonholomorphic-fourier-basis-decaying](#QM-3-nonholomorphic-fourier-basis-decaying), [QM.3/nonholomorphic-fourier-basis-growing](#QM-3-nonholomorphic-fourier-basis-growing).

Construction or proof route:

1. Holomorphy: f is C² and Δ_k f = 0, so ξ_k f is holomorphic (QM.3/xi-holomorphic-iff-harmonic).
2. Invariance: (ξ_k f)|_{2−k}γ = ξ_k(f|_kγ) = ξ_k f for γ ∈ Γ (QM.3/xi-slash-equivariance).
3. Growth at a cusp c = g∞ (g ∈ SL₂(ℤ)): f|_kg ∈ H_k(g^{−1}Γg); expand it by QM.3/harmonic-fourier-coefficient-ode; ξ_k kills the α-terms and maps the β-terms to β̄₀(1−k), −β̄_n(4π|n|/h)^{1−k}e(|n|τ/h) (n < 0) and β̄_n(2πn/h)^{1−k}e(−nτ/h) (n > 0) (QM.3/nonholomorphic-fourier-basis-decaying/-growing); by QM.3/harmonic-coefficients-eventually-zero only finitely many negative powers occur, so (ξ_k f)|_{2−k}g has exponential growth at ∞; any other g′ with g′∞ = c differs by an upper-triangular matrix.
4. Conjugate-linearity from xiOperator_add.

Uses that determine the API:

- Bruinier–Funke Thm. 3.7, Cor. 3.8: the surjection onto M^!_{2−k} and S_{2−k}
- Bruinier–Funke (3.9): {g, f} = (g, ξ_k f)
- Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades Prop. 5.1, §6: ξ_{2−k}Q(−m, k, N) is a multiple of the Poincaré series P(m, k, N)

Named declarations and API:

- `HarmonicMaassForm.xi` (constructor): The conjugate-linear map ξ_k : H_k(Γ) →ₗ⋆[ℂ] M^!_{2−k}(Γ).
- `HarmonicMaassForm.coe_xi` (simp): The underlying function of ξ_k f is xiOperator k f.
- `HarmonicMaassForm.xi_toHarmonic` (simp): ξ_k(toHarmonic g) = 0 for g ∈ M^!_k(Γ).
- `HarmonicMaassForm.xi_ofLe` (functoriality): ξ commutes with restriction to an arithmetic subgroup Γ′ ≤ Γ.

Unit tests:

- `xi_e2Star_test` (computation): ξ_2(E₂*) is the constant weakly holomorphic form 3/π of weight 0 for SL₂(ℤ).
- `xi_toHarmonic_test` (degenerate): ξ_k(f) = 0 for every f in the image of M^!_k(Γ) → H_k(Γ).
- `xi_smul_test` (non-example): ξ_k(i·f) = −i·ξ_k(f): the map is conjugate-linear, and for E₂* one gets ξ_2(i E₂*) = −3i/π ≠ 3i/π.

Acceptance checks:

- ξ_2(E₂*) = 3/π, the constant function, an element of M_0(SL₂(ℤ)) ⊆ M^!_0(SL₂(ℤ)).
- ξ_k vanishes on the image of M^!_k(Γ).

<a id="QM-3-xi-kernel-weakly-holomorphic"></a>

### ker ξ_k = M^!_k(Γ)

**Theorem** (`QM.3/xi-kernel-weakly-holomorphic`). For Γ arithmetic with Γ.HasDetOne and k ∈ ℤ, k ≠ 1, the kernel of ξ_k : H_k(Γ) → M^!_{2−k}(Γ) is the image of M^!_k(Γ) (Bruinier–Funke Prop. 3.2).

Hypotheses and conventions:

- As in QM.3/xi-map.

Source support:

- [bruinier-funke-2004](#reference-bruinier-funke-2004), Prop. 3.2, p. 10. Exactly the statement (scalar case).

Direct prerequisites: [QM.3/xi-map](#QM-3-xi-map), [QM.3/xi-operator](#QM-3-xi-operator).

Construction or proof route:

1. ξ_k f = 0 ⟺ ∂_τ̄ f = 0 on ℍ ⟺ f holomorphic (xiOperator_eq_zero_iff).
2. A holomorphic f ∈ H_k(Γ) is slash-invariant with exponential growth at the cusps, i.e. lies in M^!_k(Γ); conversely xi_toHarmonic.

Acceptance checks:

- E₂* ∉ ker ξ_2 while 1/Δ ∈ ker ξ_{−12}.

<a id="QM-3-harmonic-maass-form-plus-space"></a>

### The subspace H_k^+(Γ) = ξ_k^{−1}(S_{2−k}(Γ))

**Definition** (`QM.3/harmonic-maass-form-plus-space`). For Γ arithmetic with Γ.HasDetOne and k ∈ ℤ, k ≠ 1: H_k^+(Γ) := {f ∈ H_k(Γ) : ξ_k f is a cusp form}, the preimage of S_{2−k}(Γ) (Mathlib's CuspForm Γ (2 − k)) under ξ_k. It is a ℂ-subspace (ξ_k is additive and S_{2−k} is stable under conjugate scalars). Equivalently (QM.3/plus-space-principal-part-characterisation) at every cusp f minus a Laurent polynomial in q^{−1} decays exponentially — the definition of Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades' H_k.

Hypotheses and conventions:

- As in QM.3/xi-map.

Source support:

- [bruinier-funke-2004](#reference-bruinier-funke-2004), p. 11. Exactly the definition.
- [bruinier-funke-2004](#reference-bruinier-funke-2004), p. 11. API items range_toHarmonic_le_plusSpace and plusSpace_eq_range_of_two_le.

Direct prerequisites: [QM.3/xi-map](#QM-3-xi-map), `mathlib:CuspForm`, `tauceti:ModularForm.subsingleton_of_neg_weight`.

Construction or proof route:

1. Define as the Submodule {f | ∃ g : CuspForm Γ (2−k), ⇑g = ⇑(ξ_k f)}; closure under c·: ξ(cf) = c̄ξf and c̄g is a cusp form.
2. M^!_k(Γ) ⊆ H_k^+(Γ) since ξ vanishes there.
3. k ≥ 2: S_{2−k}(Γ) = 0 (weight ≤ 0 cusp forms vanish: negative weight by ModularForm.subsingleton_of_neg_weight in Tau Ceti, weight 0 by constancy), so H_k^+(Γ) = M^!_k(Γ).

Uses that determine the API:

- Bruinier–Funke Thm. 3.6, Cor. 3.8(2), (3.9): domain of the pairing and middle term of the second exact sequence
- Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades §§1–6: their H_{2−k}(Γ₀(N), χ): Fourier expansion (1.2), D^{k−1}, Maass–Poincaré series
- QM.4, QM.5: the holomorphic part of an element of H_k^+ is a mock modular form with shadow ξ_k f

Named declarations and API:

- `HarmonicMaassForm.plusSpace` (data): The submodule ξ_k^{−1}(S_{2−k}(Γ)) of H_k(Γ).
- `HarmonicMaassForm.mem_plusSpace_iff` (characterisation): f ∈ H_k^+(Γ) ↔ ∃ g : CuspForm Γ (2−k), ⇑g = ξ_k f.
- `HarmonicMaassForm.range_toHarmonic_le_plusSpace` (relation): M^!_k(Γ) ≤ H_k^+(Γ).
- `HarmonicMaassForm.plusSpace_eq_range_of_two_le` (other): For k ≥ 2: H_k^+(Γ) = M^!_k(Γ).

Unit tests:

- `e2Star_not_mem_plusSpace_test` (non-example): E₂* ∈ H_2(SL₂(ℤ)) but E₂* ∉ H_2^+(SL₂(ℤ)).
- `toHarmonic_mem_plusSpace_test` (degenerate): Every weakly holomorphic form lies in H_k^+(Γ).
- `plusSpace_eq_range_of_two_le_test` (compatibility): For k ≥ 2, H_k^+(Γ) equals the image of M^!_k(Γ).

Acceptance checks:

- E₂* ∉ H_2^+(SL₂(ℤ)) since ξ_2E₂* = 3/π is not a cusp form; M^!_k ⊆ H_k^+; Q(−m, k, N) ∈ H_{2−k}^+(Γ₀(N)).

<a id="QM-3-harmonic-maass-form-fourier-expansion"></a>

### Fourier expansion of f ∈ H_k^+(Γ)

**Theorem** (`QM.3/harmonic-maass-form-fourier-expansion`). Let Γ be arithmetic with Γ.HasDetOne, k ∈ ℤ, k ≠ 1, h = Γ.strictWidthInfty and f ∈ H_k^+(Γ). There are N ∈ ℕ and a⁺, a⁻ : ℤ → ℂ with a⁺(n) = 0 for n < −N, a⁻(n) = 0 for n ≥ 0, such that for all τ ∈ ℍ, f(τ) = Σ_{n∈ℤ} a⁺(n)e(nτ/h) + Σ_{n<0} a⁻(n)Γ(1−k, 4π|n|v/h)e(nτ/h), both series converging absolutely and locally uniformly. The coefficients are unique; a⁺(n) = lim_{v→∞} a(n; v)e^{2πnv/h}. (Bruinier–Funke (3.2) restricted to H^+; Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades (1.2) with h = 1 and weight 2 − k.)

Hypotheses and conventions:

- k ≠ 1; f ∈ H_k^+ (for f ∈ H_k \ H_k^+ the constant term v^{1−k} and the growing terms ψ_n also occur, see QM.3/harmonic-fourier-coefficient-ode).

Source support:

- [bruinier-funke-2004](#reference-bruinier-funke-2004), (3.2a), (3.2b), p. 9. The decomposition; for f ∈ H^+ only n < 0 survives in f^− (BF p. 11).
- [bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008](#reference-bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008), (1.2), p. 2. The same statement in weight 2 − k, width 1 (their H is our H^+).

Direct prerequisites: [QM.3/harmonic-maass-form-plus-space](#QM-3-harmonic-maass-form-plus-space), [QM.3/harmonic-fourier-coefficient-ode](#QM-3-harmonic-fourier-coefficient-ode), [QM.3/harmonic-coefficients-eventually-zero](#QM-3-harmonic-coefficients-eventually-zero), [QM.3/nonholomorphic-fourier-basis-decaying](#QM-3-nonholomorphic-fourier-basis-decaying), [QM.3/nonholomorphic-fourier-basis-growing](#QM-3-nonholomorphic-fourier-basis-growing), [QM.3/nonholomorphic-coefficient-bound](#QM-3-nonholomorphic-coefficient-bound).

Construction or proof route:

1. Expand by QM.3/harmonic-fourier-coefficient-ode with coefficients α_n, β_n.
2. ξ_k f = Σ_n (ξ of the β-terms) is a cusp form; its constant term is β̄₀(1−k) and its negative-index terms are β̄_n(2πn/h)^{1−k} (n > 0); uniqueness of Fourier coefficients of ξ_k f gives β₀ = 0 (k ≠ 1) and β_n = 0 for n > 0.
3. Set a⁺ = α, a⁻ = β; a⁺(n) = 0 for n ≪ 0 by QM.3/harmonic-coefficients-eventually-zero.
4. Convergence: Σ_{n<0}|a⁻(n)Γ(1−k, 4π|n|v/h)e(nτ/h)| converges since |a⁻(n)| = O(|n|^{k/2}) (QM.3/nonholomorphic-coefficient-bound) and the basis functions are O(v^{−k}e^{−2π|n|v/h}); the a⁺-series is then the difference of two convergent Fourier series.
5. The limit formula for a⁺(n): Γ(1−k, x) → 0 as x → ∞ and v^{1−k}-term absent.

Acceptance checks:

- For f ∈ M^!_k(Γ) this is the Laurent expansion with a⁻ = 0.
- For Q(−m, k, 1) (k even ≥ 4): a⁺(−m) = 1, a⁻(−m) = −1/(k−2)!, a⁺(0) given by BOR Prop. 6.2 (for m = 1, k = 12: a⁺(0) = −65520/691).

<a id="QM-3-holomorphic-part"></a>

### Holomorphic and non-holomorphic parts f⁺, f⁻ (mock modular forms)

**Definition** (`QM.3/holomorphic-part`). For f ∈ H_k^+(Γ) (Γ arithmetic, Γ.HasDetOne, k ∈ ℤ, k ≠ 1, h = Γ.strictWidthInfty), with a⁺, a⁻ as in QM.3/harmonic-maass-form-fourier-expansion: the holomorphic part f⁺(τ) := Σ_n a⁺(n)e(nτ/h) and the non-holomorphic part f⁻ := f − f⁺ = Σ_{n<0} a⁻(n)Γ(1−k, 4π|n|v/h)e(nτ/h). Coefficient functionals: a⁺(n) = lim_{v→∞} (h^{−1}∫_0^h f(u+iv)e(−nu/h)du)·e^{2πnv/h} (defined for every function) and a⁻(n) = the coefficient of Γ(1−k, 4π|n|v/h)e(nτ/h). f⁺ is a mock modular form in Zagier's sense: its shadow is ξ_k f, a cusp form of weight 2 − k.

Hypotheses and conventions:

- Defined at the cusp ∞ with the width of Γ; at another cusp σ∞ apply the definition to f|_kσ ∈ H_k^+(σ^{−1}Γσ).
- Normalisation pinned: f⁺ carries all holomorphic terms including the constant term a⁺(0); f⁻ has no constant term.

Source support:

- [bruinier-funke-2004](#reference-bruinier-funke-2004), (3.2a), (3.2b), p. 9. f⁺ and f⁻ as in (3.2a), (3.2b).
- [bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008](#reference-bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008), (1.4), (1.5), p. 2. Same definitions in weight 2 − k.

Direct prerequisites: [QM.3/harmonic-maass-form-fourier-expansion](#QM-3-harmonic-maass-form-fourier-expansion), [QM.3/harmonic-maass-form-plus-space](#QM-3-harmonic-maass-form-plus-space), [QM.3/xi-operator](#QM-3-xi-operator), [QM.3/upper-incomplete-gamma](#QM-3-upper-incomplete-gamma).

Construction or proof route:

1. Define holoCoeff f n by the limit formula (a real definition, valid for any function); holomorphicPart f τ := Σ' n, holoCoeff f n · e(nτ/h).
2. By QM.3/harmonic-maass-form-fourier-expansion the limit exists and equals a⁺(n), and f = f⁺ + f⁻.
3. f⁺ is holomorphic on ℍ (locally uniform limit of holomorphic partial sums with finitely many negative terms).
4. ξ_k f = ξ_k f⁻ since ξ_k f⁺ = 0; f⁻ = O(v^{−k}e^{−2πv/h}) as v → ∞.

Uses that determine the API:

- Bruinier–Funke (3.6), Prop. 3.5: the principal part of f⁺ determines the pairing {g, f}
- Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades Theorem 1.1: D^{k−1}f = D^{k−1}f⁺ = Σ c⁺(n)n^{k−1}q^n
- QM.4 (Zwegers): the mock theta functions are holomorphic parts: F₇ = H₇ + G₇ with G₇ non-holomorphic
- QM.5: radial limits of f⁺ at rationals (quantum modular forms)

Named declarations and API:

- `HarmonicMaassForm.holoCoeff` (data): a⁺(n) := lim_{v→∞} h^{−1}∫_0^h f(u+iv)e(−nu/h)du · e^{2πnv/h}.
- `HarmonicMaassForm.nonHoloCoeff` (data): a⁻(n), the coefficient of Γ(1−k, 4π|n|v/h)e(nτ/h) (0 for n ≥ 0).
- `HarmonicMaassForm.holomorphicPart` (data): f⁺(τ) = Σ' n, a⁺(n)e(nτ/h).
- `HarmonicMaassForm.nonHolomorphicPart` (data): f⁻ = f − f⁺.
- `HarmonicMaassForm.holomorphicPart_add_nonHolomorphicPart` (characterisation): f = f⁺ + f⁻.
- `HarmonicMaassForm.mdifferentiable_holomorphicPart` (other): f⁺ is holomorphic on ℍ.
- `HarmonicMaassForm.xi_nonHolomorphicPart` (relation): ξ_k f = ξ_k f⁻.
- `HarmonicMaassForm.holomorphicPart_toHarmonic` (compatibility): For g ∈ M^!_k(Γ), (toHarmonic g)⁺ = g.

Unit tests:

- `holomorphicPart_toHarmonic_test` (degenerate): For g ∈ M^!_k(Γ), the holomorphic part of its image in H_k^+(Γ) is g itself.
- `holoCoeff_maassPoincare_test` (computation): For the Maass–Poincaré series Q(−m, k, N): holoCoeff(Q)(−m) = 1 and holoCoeff(Q)(n) = 0 for n < −m.
- `holomorphicPart_not_invariant_test` (non-example): The holomorphic part Q⁺ of Q = Q(−1, 12, 1) is not invariant under |_{−10}SL₂(ℤ): otherwise Q⁻ = Q − Q⁺ would lie in H^+_{−10}(SL₂(ℤ)) with all holomorphic coefficients 0, so {Δ, Q⁻} = 0 (QM.3/bruinier-funke-pairing-formula), i.e. (Δ, ξQ⁻) = 0 with ξQ⁻ = ξQ ∈ S₁₂ = ℂΔ, forcing ξQ = 0, which contradicts QM.3/xi-maass-poincare-series.
- `holomorphicPart_add_test` (characterisation): f = f⁺ + f⁻ pointwise, and f⁻ → 0 as Im τ → ∞.

Acceptance checks:

- For f ∈ M^!_k(Γ): f⁺ = f and f⁻ = 0.
- For Q(−m, k, N): f⁺ = q^{−m} + O(1) at ∞.

<a id="QM-3-principal-part"></a>

### The principal part P(f)

**Definition** (`QM.3/principal-part`). For f ∈ H_k^+(Γ) as in QM.3/holomorphic-part, P(f) := Σ_{n≤0} a⁺(n)T^n ∈ ℂ[T, T^{−1}] (a Laurent polynomial by QM.3/harmonic-coefficients-eventually-zero), read as the Fourier polynomial P(f)(τ) = Σ_{n≤0} a⁺(n)e(nτ/h) (Bruinier–Funke (3.6)). It includes the constant term a⁺(0).

Hypotheses and conventions:

- At the cusp ∞ with the width h of Γ; at σ∞ use f|_kσ.

Source support:

- [bruinier-funke-2004](#reference-bruinier-funke-2004), (3.6), p. 11. Exactly the definition and the decay property.

Direct prerequisites: [QM.3/holomorphic-part](#QM-3-holomorphic-part), [QM.3/harmonic-coefficients-eventually-zero](#QM-3-harmonic-coefficients-eventually-zero), `mathlib:LaurentPolynomial`.

Construction or proof route:

1. Finite support: a⁺(n) = 0 for n < −N.
2. Build the Laurent polynomial Σ_{−N≤n≤0} a⁺(n)T^n (Mathlib's LaurentPolynomial).
3. Linearity from the linearity of the coefficient functionals.

Uses that determine the API:

- Bruinier–Funke Prop. 3.5: {g, f} = Σ_{n≤0} a⁺(n)b(−n) depends only on P(f)
- Bruinier–Funke Prop. 3.11: every Fourier polynomial with negative exponents is a principal part up to constants
- Borcherds, GKZ Thm 3.1: the obstruction space for principal parts of weakly holomorphic forms
- Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades §2 (iii): their growth condition f − P_f = O(e^{−εy})

Named declarations and API:

- `HarmonicMaassForm.principalPart` (data): P(f) ∈ LaurentPolynomial ℂ.
- `HarmonicMaassForm.principalPart_coeff` (characterisation): coeff P(f) n = a⁺(n) for n ≤ 0 and 0 for n > 0.
- `HarmonicMaassForm.principalPart_add` (simp): P(f + g) = P(f) + P(g), P(cf) = cP(f).
- `HarmonicMaassForm.sub_principalPart_isBigO` (other): ∃ε > 0: f(τ) − P(f)(e(τ/h)) = O(e^{−εv}) as v → ∞.

Unit tests:

- `principalPart_inv_discriminant_test` (computation): P(1/Δ) = T^{−1} + 24.
- `principalPart_E4_test` (computation): P(E₄) = 1.
- `principalPart_discriminant_test` (degenerate): P(Δ) = 0 (cusp forms have zero principal part).
- `principalPart_ne_nonHolo_test` (non-example): For Q(−m, k, N) the principal part is T^{−m} + a⁺(0); the non-holomorphic term −Γ(k−1, 4πmv)q^{−m}/(k−2)! does not contribute, although it is also of order q^{−m} in the exponent of e(·).

Acceptance checks:

- P(1/Δ) = T^{−1} + 24, P(E₄) = 1, P(Δ) = 0.
- f − P(f)(q_h) = O(e^{−εv}) for f ∈ H_k^+ (BF p. 11).

<a id="QM-3-plus-space-principal-part-characterisation"></a>

### H_k^+ via exponential decay after removing a principal part

**Lemma** (`QM.3/plus-space-principal-part-characterisation`). Let Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) have finite index, k ∈ ℤ, k ≠ 1, f ∈ H_k(Γ). Then f ∈ H_k^+(Γ) if and only if for every σ ∈ SL₂(ℤ) there are a Laurent polynomial P_σ ∈ ℂ[T^{−1}] and ε > 0 with (f|_kσ)(τ) − P_σ(e(τ/h_σ)) = O(e^{−εv}) as v → ∞, h_σ the width of σ^{−1}Γσ at ∞. This is the definition of Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades' space H_k(Γ₀(N), χ) (their condition (iii)), so their H_k is BF's H_k^+.

Hypotheses and conventions:

- Finite-index Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ), so every cusp is σ∞ with σ ∈ SL₂(ℤ).

Source support:

- [bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008](#reference-bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008), §2 (iii), p. 6. The right-hand side of the equivalence.
- [bruinier-funke-2004](#reference-bruinier-funke-2004), p. 11. The equivalence, asserted by BF.

Direct prerequisites: [QM.3/harmonic-maass-form-plus-space](#QM-3-harmonic-maass-form-plus-space), [QM.3/harmonic-maass-form-fourier-expansion](#QM-3-harmonic-maass-form-fourier-expansion), [QM.3/harmonic-fourier-coefficient-ode](#QM-3-harmonic-fourier-coefficient-ode), [QM.3/xi-slash-equivariance](#QM-3-xi-slash-equivariance), [QM.3/principal-part](#QM-3-principal-part).

Construction or proof route:

1. ⇒: f|_kσ ∈ H_k^+(σ^{−1}Γσ) since ξ_k(f|_kσ) = (ξ_kf)|_{2−k}σ is a cusp form for σ^{−1}Γσ; its expansion (QM.3/harmonic-maass-form-fourier-expansion) minus its principal part is Σ_{n>0}a⁺(n)q_h^n + Σ_{n<0}a⁻(n)Γ(1−k, 4π|n|v/h)q_h^n = O(e^{−εv}).
2. ⇐: in the expansion of QM.3/harmonic-fourier-coefficient-ode for f|_kσ, the terms β₀v^{1−k} (k ≠ 1) and β_nψ_n (n > 0) do not decay and are not Laurent polynomials in q, so decay forces β₀ = 0 and β_n = 0 for n > 0; then ξ_k(f|_kσ) has only positive powers of q, i.e. ξ_k f vanishes at every cusp.

Acceptance checks:

- E₂* fails the condition at ∞: E₂* − 1 = −3/(πv) + O(e^{−2πv}) is not O(e^{−εv}).

<a id="QM-3-xi-fourier-expansion"></a>

### Fourier expansion of ξ_k f

**Lemma** (`QM.3/xi-fourier-expansion`). For f ∈ H_k^+(Γ) with expansion as in QM.3/harmonic-maass-form-fourier-expansion: ξ_k f(τ) = −Σ_{n<0} \overline{a⁻(n)}(4π|n|/h)^{1−k} e(|n|τ/h). Equivalently, with b(m) the coefficients of the cusp form ξ_k f: b(m) = −\overline{a⁻(−m)}(4πm/h)^{1−k} for m ≥ 1 (Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades (1.3), with h = 1 and weight 2 − k). This corrects the constant in Bruinier–Funke Lemma 3.1 (factor 1, not 2; sourceIssue E401).

Hypotheses and conventions:

- k ∈ ℤ, k ≠ 1, f ∈ H_k^+(Γ).

Source support:

- [bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008](#reference-bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008), (1.3), p. 2. Exactly the statement (weight 2 − k, width 1).
- [bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008](#reference-bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008), proof of Thm 1.3, p. 11. Records the correction of BF Lemma 3.1 (E401).

Direct prerequisites: [QM.3/harmonic-maass-form-fourier-expansion](#QM-3-harmonic-maass-form-fourier-expansion), [QM.3/nonholomorphic-fourier-basis-decaying](#QM-3-nonholomorphic-fourier-basis-decaying), [QM.3/xi-map](#QM-3-xi-map).

Construction or proof route:

1. Apply ξ_k termwise (locally uniform convergence of the series and of its ∂̄-derivatives on compacta) and use QM.3/nonholomorphic-fourier-basis-decaying.
2. Conjugate-linearity of ξ_k turns a⁻(n) into \overline{a⁻(n)}.

Acceptance checks:

- For Q(−m, k, N): a⁻(−m) = −1/(k−2)! gives the leading coefficient (4πm)^{k−1}/(k−2)! of ξ_{2−k}Q(−m, k, N), matching BOR §6.2.

<a id="QM-3-harmonic-growth-near-real-axis"></a>

### Growth of harmonic Maass forms towards the real axis

**Lemma** (`QM.3/harmonic-growth-near-real-axis`). Let Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) have finite index and f ∈ H_k(Γ). Then there are A, C > 0 with |f(u + iv)| ≤ A e^{C/v} for all u ∈ ℝ and 0 < v ≤ 1 (Bruinier–Funke Lemma 3.3). (The same bound for f⁺, f⁻ is part of QM.3/holomorphic-coefficient-bound.)

Hypotheses and conventions:

- Γ of finite index in SL₂(ℤ) (finitely many cosets).

Source support:

- [bruinier-funke-2004](#reference-bruinier-funke-2004), Lemma 3.3, p. 11. Exactly the statement.

Direct prerequisites: [QM.3/harmonic-maass-form](#QM-3-harmonic-maass-form), `mathlib:ModularGroup.exists_smul_mem_fd`, `mathlib:ModularGroup.fd`, `mathlib:ModularForm.slash_def`.

Construction or proof route:

1. For τ = u + iv with v ≤ 1 choose γ = (a b; c d) ∈ SL₂(ℤ) with w := γτ in the standard fundamental domain (ModularGroup.exists_smul_mem_fd), so Im w ≥ √3/2.
2. Then f(τ) = j(γ, τ)^{−k}·(f|_kγ^{−1})(w) with j(γ, τ) = cτ + d, and f|_kγ^{−1} = f|_kγ₀ for γ₀ in a finite set R of representatives of Γ\SL₂(ℤ) (f is Γ-invariant).
3. Im w = v/|cτ + d|² ≤ 1/v if c ≠ 0 and Im w = v ≤ 1 if c = 0; hence √3/2 ≤ Im w ≤ 1/v and |j(γ, τ)|^{−k} = (Im w/v)^{k/2} ≤ A₁v^{−|k|}.
4. Each f|_kγ₀ (γ₀ ∈ R) is continuous with exponential growth at ∞, so |(f|_kγ₀)(w)| ≤ A₂e^{C Im w} on the fundamental domain; together |f(τ)| ≤ A₁A₂v^{−|k|}e^{C/v} ≤ A e^{(C+1)/v}.
5. The constant C is uniform because R is finite.

Acceptance checks:

- For f = 1/Δ: |1/Δ(iv)| = v^{12}|1/Δ(i/v)| grows like v^{12}e^{2π/v} as v → 0.

<a id="QM-3-nonholomorphic-coefficient-bound"></a>

### Polynomial bound for the non-holomorphic coefficients a⁻(n)

**Lemma** (`QM.3/nonholomorphic-coefficient-bound`). Let Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) have finite index, k ∈ ℤ, k ≠ 1, f ∈ H_k^+(Γ), and let β_n (n < 0) be the coefficients of the decaying basis functions in QM.3/harmonic-fourier-coefficient-ode (width h). If b(m) (m ≥ 1) are the Fourier coefficients of the cusp form ξ_k f, then b(m) = −\overline{β_{−m}}(4πm/h)^{1−k}, and consequently β_{−m} = O(m^{k/2}) as m → ∞ (Bruinier–Funke Lemma 3.4, second part).

Hypotheses and conventions:

- f ∈ H_k^+; the identity is proved mode by mode, before the full expansion is known to converge.

Source support:

- [bruinier-funke-2004](#reference-bruinier-funke-2004), Lemma 3.4, p. 11. Exactly the bound.
- [bruinier-funke-2004](#reference-bruinier-funke-2004), proof of Lemma 3.4, p. 12. The proof, via (3.7) (whose constant carries the factor-2 slip of Lemma 3.1, E401; the bound is unaffected).

Direct prerequisites: [QM.3/harmonic-fourier-coefficient-ode](#QM-3-harmonic-fourier-coefficient-ode), [QM.3/nonholomorphic-fourier-basis-decaying](#QM-3-nonholomorphic-fourier-basis-decaying), [QM.3/harmonic-maass-form-plus-space](#QM-3-harmonic-maass-form-plus-space), [QM.3/xi-map](#QM-3-xi-map), `mathlib:CuspFormClass.qExpansion_isBigO`, `mathlib:UpperHalfPlane.qExpansion`.

Construction or proof route:

1. The m-th Fourier coefficient (in u) of ξ_k f at height v is ξ_k applied to the (−m)-th Fourier mode of f: differentiation under the integral sign for the C¹ periodic function f(· + iv) and ξ_k f = 2iv^k·conj(∂̄f).
2. By QM.3/harmonic-fourier-coefficient-ode and QM.3/nonholomorphic-fourier-basis-decaying (α-terms are holomorphic, killed by ξ) this is −\overline{β_{−m}}(4πm/h)^{1−k}e(mτ/h); compare with b(m)e(mτ/h).
3. Hecke's bound b(m) = O(m^{(2−k)/2}) for the cusp form ξ_k f (Mathlib CuspFormClass.qExpansion_isBigO, width h) gives |β_{−m}| = O(m^{(2−k)/2 − (1−k)}) = O(m^{k/2}).

Acceptance checks:

- For f ∈ M^!_k(Γ) all β_n vanish, matching ξ_k f = 0.
- For Q(−m, k, N) in weight 2 − k: β_{−m} = −1/(k−2)! gives b(m) = (4πm)^{k−1}/(k−2)!, the leading coefficient of ξ_{2−k}Q(−m, k, N) = (4πm)^{k−1}/(k−2)!·P(m, k, N) (BOR §6.2).

<a id="QM-3-holomorphic-coefficient-bound"></a>

### Subexponential bound for the holomorphic coefficients a⁺(n)

**Lemma** (`QM.3/holomorphic-coefficient-bound`). Let Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) have finite index, k ∈ ℤ, k ≠ 1, f ∈ H_k^+(Γ). Then f⁺ and f⁻ satisfy the bound of QM.3/harmonic-growth-near-real-axis, and there is C > 0 with a⁺(n) = O(e^{C√n}) as n → +∞ (Bruinier–Funke Lemma 3.4, first part).

Hypotheses and conventions:

- f ∈ H_k^+(Γ).

Source support:

- [bruinier-funke-2004](#reference-bruinier-funke-2004), Lemma 3.4, p. 11. The a⁺ bound (the a⁻ bound on H^+ is superseded by QM.3/nonholomorphic-coefficient-bound).
- [bruinier-funke-2004](#reference-bruinier-funke-2004), proof of Lemma 3.4, p. 12. The bound for f⁺ and f⁻ (first proof step).

Direct prerequisites: [QM.3/harmonic-growth-near-real-axis](#QM-3-harmonic-growth-near-real-axis), [QM.3/nonholomorphic-coefficient-bound](#QM-3-nonholomorphic-coefficient-bound), [QM.3/harmonic-maass-form-fourier-expansion](#QM-3-harmonic-maass-form-fourier-expansion), [QM.3/holomorphic-part](#QM-3-holomorphic-part), [QM.3/upper-incomplete-gamma](#QM-3-upper-incomplete-gamma).

Construction or proof route:

1. For integer k ≠ 1 the integral definition and recurrence of Γ give the uniform bound |Γ(1−k, x)e^{x/2}| ≤ C(1 + x^{−max(k,0)})e^{−x/4} for x > 0: bound the integral separately on 0 < x ≤ 1 and x ≥ 1, absorbing the large-x polynomial into e^{x/4}. The asymptotic C x^{−k}e^{−x/2} alone is not a bound for small x when k ≤ 0. Multiply by |a⁻(−m)| = O(m^{k/2}) (QM.3/nonholomorphic-coefficient-bound) and sum at x = 4πmv/h. Exponentially weighted power sums give |f⁻(τ)| ≤ A v^{−N} ≤ A′e^{1/v} for 0 < v ≤ 1 and some integer N; then f⁺ = f − f⁻ satisfies |f⁺| ≤ A e^{C/v} (QM.3/harmonic-growth-near-real-axis).
2. a⁺(n) = h^{−1}∫_0^h f⁺(u + iv)e(−n(u + iv)/h)du for every v > 0, so |a⁺(n)| ≤ A e^{C/v}e^{2πnv/h}; take v = 1/√n.

Acceptance checks:

- For Q(−1, 12, 1): a⁺(n) grows like const·n^{−11/2}·I_{11}(4π√n), i.e. like e^{4π√n}n^{−23/4}, consistent with O(e^{C√n}).

<a id="QM-3-truncated-fundamental-domain-stokes"></a>

### Stokes' theorem on the truncated fundamental domain

**Lemma** (`QM.3/truncated-fundamental-domain-stokes`). Let F_T := {τ ∈ ℍ : |τ| ≥ 1, |Re τ| ≤ 1/2, Im τ ≤ T} (T > 1) and let G be a C¹ function on a neighbourhood of F_T. Then ∫_{F_T} ∂_τ̄ G(τ) du dv = (1/(2i))∮_{∂F_T} G(τ) dτ, with ∂F_T positively oriented (the boundary path is Tau Ceti's TauCeti.ModularForm.fdBoundary T). In the form used by Bruinier–Funke: for the 1-form ω = G dτ, dω = ∂_τ̄G dτ̄ ∧ dτ = 2i ∂_τ̄G du ∧ dv.

Hypotheses and conventions:

- G of class C¹ on an open set containing F_T; T > 1.

Source support:

- [bruinier-funke-2004](#reference-bruinier-funke-2004), proof of Prop. 3.5, p. 12. The Stokes step used in Prop. 3.5, on exactly this domain.

Direct prerequisites: [QM.3/wirtinger-derivatives](#QM-3-wirtinger-derivatives), `tauceti:TauCeti.ModularForm.fdBoundary`, `mathlib:MeasureTheory.integral_prod`, `mathlib:intervalIntegral.integral_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt`, `mathlib:intervalIntegral.hasDerivAt_integral_of_dominated_loc_of_deriv_le`.

Construction or proof route:

1. F_T = {(u, v) : |u| ≤ ½, φ(u) ≤ v ≤ T} with φ(u) = √(1 − u²) is vertically simple.
2. ∫∫ ∂_v G dv du = ∫_{−1/2}^{1/2}[G(u, T) − G(u, φ(u))]du by the fundamental theorem of calculus in v and Fubini (MeasureTheory.integral_prod).
3. ∫∫ ∂_u G dv du: differentiate u ↦ ∫_{φ(u)}^T G(u, v)dv (Leibniz rule with variable lower limit) and integrate in u: ∫∫∂_uG = [∫_{φ(u)}^T G dv]_{u=−1/2}^{1/2} + ∫ G(u, φ(u))φ′(u)du.
4. Combine ∂̄ = ½(∂_u + i∂_v) and compare with the four boundary pieces of fdBoundary T (right side, top, left side, arc).

Acceptance checks:

- For G = τ̄ (∂̄G = 1): (1/(2i))∮_{∂F_T} τ̄ dτ equals the Euclidean area T − π/6 − √3/4 of F_T.
- For holomorphic G both sides vanish (Cauchy's theorem on F_T).

<a id="QM-3-bruinier-funke-pairing"></a>

### The Bruinier–Funke pairing {g, f}

**Definition** (`QM.3/bruinier-funke-pairing`). Let Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) have finite index, k ∈ ℤ, k ≠ 1, κ := 2 − k. For g ∈ M_κ(Γ) (Mathlib's ModularForm Γ κ) and f ∈ H_k^+(Γ): {g, f} := (g, ξ_k f)_κ, the Petersson product of the modular form g with the cusp form ξ_k f, (g, h)_κ := Σ_{q ∈ SL₂(ℤ)/Γ̃} ∫_{F} (g|_κq^{−1})(τ)·\overline{(h|_κq^{−1})(τ)}·v^κ dμ(τ), where Γ̃ = Γ·{±I}, F = ModularGroup.fd and dμ = du dv/v² is Mathlib's measure on ℍ (an unnormalised integral over Γ̃\ℍ). In Tau Ceti's notation (g, h)_κ = Σ_q UpperHalfPlane.peterssonInner κ F (h|q^{−1}) (g|q^{−1}), which for a cusp form g is CuspForm.peterssonInnerCosets h g. The pairing is ℂ-bilinear (ξ_k is conjugate-linear and the Petersson product conjugate-linear in h).

Hypotheses and conventions:

- Γ of finite index in SL₂(ℤ) (viewed in GL₂(ℝ)); k ≠ 1.
- Convention pinned: linear in g, and linear in f; the Petersson product is not normalised by the index.

Source support:

- [bruinier-funke-2004](#reference-bruinier-funke-2004), (3.9), p. 12. Exactly the definition (scalar case).
- [bruinier-funke-2004](#reference-bruinier-funke-2004), (3.4), p. 10. The Petersson product, linear in the first variable.

Direct prerequisites: [QM.3/xi-map](#QM-3-xi-map), [QM.3/harmonic-maass-form-plus-space](#QM-3-harmonic-maass-form-plus-space), `mathlib:ModularForm`, `mathlib:ModularGroup.fd`, `tauceti:UpperHalfPlane.peterssonInner`, `tauceti:CuspForm.peterssonInnerCosets`, `tauceti:UpperHalfPlane.integrableOn_petersson_sl_smul_fd_left`, `tauceti:UpperHalfPlane.integrableOn_petersson_sl_smul_fd_right`, `tauceti:Subgroup.withCenter`.

Construction or proof route:

1. Each summand is integrable: g|q^{−1} is a modular form and (ξ_kf)|q^{−1} a cusp form for q^{−1}Γq, bounded by Tau Ceti's integrableOn_petersson_sl_smul_fd_left/right.
2. Independence of the coset representatives: g|(qδ)^{−1} = g|q^{−1} for δ ∈ Γ̃ up to the sign (−1)^κ, which cancels between g and \overline{h} since both have weight κ.
3. Bilinearity from the sesquilinearity of the integral and the conjugate-linearity of ξ_k.

Uses that determine the API:

- Bruinier–Funke Prop. 3.5: evaluated through principal parts
- Bruinier–Funke Thm. 3.6: non-degeneracy on H_k^+/M^!_k × S_κ
- Bruinier–Funke Prop. 3.11 and Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades Prop. 5.1: representing linear functionals on S_κ by harmonic Maass forms
- QM.3/level-one-plus-space-spanned-by-poincare-series: kills the difference between a form and a Poincaré combination

Named declarations and API:

- `bruinierFunkePairing` (data): {g, f} = (g, ξ_k f)_κ as a ℂ-bilinear map M_κ(Γ) × H_k^+(Γ) → ℂ.
- `bruinierFunkePairing_add_left` (structure): Bilinearity: additive and ℂ-linear in each variable.
- `bruinierFunkePairing_toHarmonic` (simp): {g, f} = 0 for f in the image of M^!_k(Γ).
- `bruinierFunkePairing_eq_peterssonInnerCosets` (compatibility): For g ∈ S_κ(Γ): {g, f} = CuspForm.peterssonInnerCosets (ξ_k f) g (Tau Ceti).

Unit tests:

- `bruinierFunkePairing_toHarmonic_test` (degenerate): {g, f} = 0 whenever f is (the image of) a weakly holomorphic form.
- `bruinierFunkePairing_maassPoincare_test` (computation): For even k ≥ 4, g ∈ S_k(SL₂(ℤ)) with coefficients b(n), and the Maass–Poincaré series Q(−m, k, 1) ∈ H_{2−k}^+(SL₂(ℤ)): {g, Q(−m, k, 1)} = b(m).
- `bruinierFunkePairing_smul_right_test` (non-example): {g, c·f} = c·{g, f} (linear, not conjugate-linear, in f although ξ_k is conjugate-linear).
- `bruinierFunkePairing_eq_peterssonInnerCosets_test` (compatibility): For g a cusp form, {g, f} equals Tau Ceti's CuspForm.peterssonInnerCosets (ξ_k f) g.

Acceptance checks:

- {g, f} = 0 for f ∈ M^!_k(Γ).
- For level one, g ∈ S_κ and Q(−m, k′, 1) with k′ = κ: {g, Q(−m)} = b_g(m), the m-th coefficient of g (QM.3/bruinier-funke-pairing-formula).

<a id="QM-3-bruinier-funke-pairing-formula"></a>

### {g, f} in terms of principal parts

**Theorem** (`QM.3/bruinier-funke-pairing-formula`). Let Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) have finite index, k ∈ ℤ, k ≠ 1, κ = 2 − k, g ∈ M_κ(Γ), f ∈ H_k^+(Γ). For each cusp c of Γ choose σ_c ∈ SL₂(ℤ) with σ_c∞ = c and let h_c be the width, a⁺_c(n) the holomorphic coefficients of f|_kσ_c and b_c(n) the coefficients of g|_κσ_c (in e(nτ/h_c)). Write w_c for the geometric cusp width (possibly h_c/2). Then {g, f} = Σ_{c ∈ Γ\ℙ¹(ℚ)} w_c Σ_{n≤0} a⁺_c(n) b_c(−n). In particular the pairing depends only on the principal parts of f at the cusps. For Γ = SL₂(ℤ): {g, f} = Σ_{n≤0} a⁺(n)b(−n) (Bruinier–Funke Prop. 3.5).

Hypotheses and conventions:

- Finite-index Γ; the choice of σ_c does not matter (another choice changes both expansions by the same translation).
- Fourier coefficients use the strict period h_c. Cusp-sum weights are w_c := widthInfty(σ_c^{−1}Γσ_c), the orbit length for Γ·{±I}; w_c = h_c at regular cusps and w_c = h_c/2 at irregular cusps.

Source support:

- [bruinier-funke-2004](#reference-bruinier-funke-2004), Prop. 3.5, p. 12. The level-one statement.
- [bruinier-funke-2004](#reference-bruinier-funke-2004), p. 12. The finite-index generalisation; the cusp-sum form is the one used by BOR Theorem 4.1.
- [bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008](#reference-bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008), Theorem 4.1, proof, p. 9. Same Stokes argument with widths w_κ at the cusps.

Direct prerequisites: [QM.3/bruinier-funke-pairing](#QM-3-bruinier-funke-pairing), [QM.3/truncated-fundamental-domain-stokes](#QM-3-truncated-fundamental-domain-stokes), [QM.3/harmonic-maass-form-fourier-expansion](#QM-3-harmonic-maass-form-fourier-expansion), [QM.3/holomorphic-part](#QM-3-holomorphic-part), [QM.3/maass-lowering-operator](#QM-3-maass-lowering-operator), `mathlib:UpperHalfPlane.qExpansion`.

Construction or proof route:

1. Pointwise: g·\overline{ξ_kf}·v^κ = g·L_kf (since \overline{ξ_kf} = v^{k−2}L_kf), and d(g f dτ) = ∂̄(gf)dτ̄∧dτ = −g L_k f dμ (g holomorphic).
2. For each coset q apply QM.3/truncated-fundamental-domain-stokes to G_q = (g|q^{−1})(f|q^{−1}) on F_T; the integral over F converges and is the limit T → ∞.
3. Sum over q ∈ SL₂(ℤ)/Γ̃: the two vertical sides cancel after reindexing q ↦ T^{−1}q (the form G_q dτ has weight 2), the arc cancels after q ↦ S^{−1}q.
4. Top edges: the cosets in one orbit of q ↦ Tq correspond to a cusp c and there are w_c of them (Γ̃ counts ±); the sum of their top integrals is (w_c/h_c)∫_0^{h_c}(g|σ_c)(f|σ_c)(u + iT)du = w_c·(constant term) = w_c Σ_{n≤0}a⁺_c(n)b_c(−n) + (terms Γ(1−k, 4π|n|T/h_c)·b_c(−n) → 0).
5. Let T → ∞.

Acceptance checks:

- For level one and f = Q(−m, κ, 1), g = E_κ (Eisenstein series, orthogonal to cusp forms): 0 = a⁺(0) + b_{E_κ}(m); for m = 1, κ = 12 this gives a⁺(0) = −65520/691, which BOR Prop. 6.2 confirms numerically (BOR's introduction prints −0.04629; sourceIssue E405).
- {g, f} = 0 for f ∈ M^!_k(Γ) gives Σ_c w_c Σ_{n≤0} a_c(n)b_c(−n) = 0, the residue theorem for f g dτ on X(Γ).

<a id="QM-3-normal-torsion-free-subgroup"></a>

### Finite-index subgroups contain a normal subgroup acting freely

**Lemma** (`QM.3/normal-torsion-free-subgroup`). Every finite-index subgroup Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) contains a subgroup Γ″ of finite index in SL₂(ℤ), normal in SL₂(ℤ), that acts freely on ℍ; one may take Γ″ = Γ(3) ∩ core(Γ), where core(Γ) = ⋂_{g} gΓg^{−1} is the normal core and Γ(3) the principal congruence subgroup of level 3.

Hypotheses and conventions:

- Γ of finite index in SL₂(ℤ).

Source support:

- [bruinier-funke-2004](#reference-bruinier-funke-2004), proof of Thm. 3.7, p. 14. The existence of such Γ″ is used without proof; this lemma supplies it.

Direct prerequisites: `mathlib:Subgroup.normalCore`, `mathlib:Subgroup.normalCore_normal`, `mathlib:Subgroup.finiteIndex_normalCore`, `mathlib:CongruenceSubgroup.Gamma`, `mathlib:CongruenceSubgroup.Gamma_normal`, `mathlib:CongruenceSubgroup.IsCongruenceSubgroup.finiteIndex`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ModularGroup.finite_stabilizer`.

Construction or proof route:

1. core(Γ) is normal of finite index (Subgroup.normalCore_normal, Subgroup.finiteIndex_normalCore); Γ(3) is normal (CongruenceSubgroup.Gamma_normal) of finite index; their intersection is normal of finite index.
2. Stabilizers of points of ℍ in SL₂(ℤ) are finite (Tau Ceti's TauCeti.ModularGroup.finite_stabilizer) and consist of ±I and elliptic elements, whose traces lie in {0, ±1}; an element of Γ(3) has trace ≡ 2 mod 3, so traces 0 and 1 are excluded; trace −1 would mean γ² + γ + I = 0 with γ = I + 3A, i.e. 3(I + 3A + 3A²) = 0, impossible mod 3; and −I ∉ Γ(3).
3. Hence the stabilizer in Γ″ of every point is trivial: Γ″ acts freely.

Acceptance checks:

- For Γ = SL₂(ℤ): Γ″ = Γ(3), of index 24, acting freely on ℍ.

<a id="QM-3-local-xi-preimage-at-cusps"></a>

### Local ξ-preimages near a cusp

**Lemma** (`QM.3/local-xi-preimage-at-cusps`). Let Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) have finite index, k ∈ ℤ, k ≠ 1, g ∈ M^!_{2−k}(Γ), σ ∈ SL₂(ℤ), h the width of σ^{−1}Γσ at ∞ and (g|_{2−k}σ)(τ) = Σ_{m≥−N} b(m)e(mτ/h). Then F_σ(τ) := Σ_{m≥1} −\overline{b(m)}(4πm/h)^{k−1}Γ(1−k, 4πmv/h)e(−mτ/h) + \overline{b(0)}(1−k)^{−1}v^{1−k} + Σ_{m=1}^{N}\overline{b(−m)}(2πm/h)^{k−1}ψ_m(τ), with ψ_m as in QM.3/nonholomorphic-fourier-basis-growing (weight k, width h), converges absolutely and locally uniformly on ℍ with all derivatives, is h-periodic and C^∞, satisfies Δ_k F_σ = 0, and ξ_k F_σ = g|_{2−k}σ on ℍ.

Hypotheses and conventions:

- k ≠ 1 (the constant term needs (1 − k)^{−1}).
- No invariance beyond the translations T^h is claimed: F_σ is only used near the cusp.

Source support:

- [bruinier-funke-2004](#reference-bruinier-funke-2004), proof of Thm. 3.7, p. 14. BF's claim that this (0,1)-form is a smooth section near the cusps is not justified (sourceIssue E406); the explicit local preimage F_σ repairs the argument near each cusp.

Direct prerequisites: [QM.3/nonholomorphic-fourier-basis-decaying](#QM-3-nonholomorphic-fourier-basis-decaying), [QM.3/nonholomorphic-fourier-basis-growing](#QM-3-nonholomorphic-fourier-basis-growing), [QM.3/weakly-holomorphic-laurent-expansion](#QM-3-weakly-holomorphic-laurent-expansion), [QM.3/xi-operator](#QM-3-xi-operator), [QM.3/upper-incomplete-gamma](#QM-3-upper-incomplete-gamma).

Construction or proof route:

1. Termwise, by QM.3/nonholomorphic-fourier-basis-decaying (ξ of the Γ-terms gives b(m)e(mτ/h) after conjugation), ξ_k(v^{1−k}) = 1 − k, and QM.3/nonholomorphic-fourier-basis-growing (ξ of ψ_m gives (2πm/h)^{1−k}e(−mτ/h)).
2. Convergence: Σ|b(m)|e^{−2πmv/h} < ∞ for every v > 0 (Laurent expansion of g|σ converges absolutely), on each compact subset of ℍ all sufficiently large m have x≥1, where |Γ(1−k, x)e^{x/2}| ≤ Cx^{−k}e^{−x/2}; the derivative series have analogous large-x bounds with polynomial factors, absorbed by comparing the Laurent expansion at half the compact set’s minimum height; finitely many smaller m are smooth.
3. ξ_k is applied termwise (locally uniform convergence of the derivative series).

Acceptance checks:

- For g = 3/π (weight 0, level one, k = 2): F = −(3/π)v^{−1}, the non-holomorphic part of E₂*.

<a id="QM-3-xi-surjective-free-normal"></a>

### ξ_k is surjective for a normal subgroup acting freely

**Theorem** (`QM.3/xi-surjective-free-normal`). Let Γ″ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) be of finite index, normal in SL₂(ℤ) and acting freely on ℍ, and k ∈ ℤ, k ≠ 1. Then ξ_k : H_k(Γ″) → M^!_{2−k}(Γ″) is surjective (Bruinier–Funke Thm. 3.7 for Γ″, repaired at the cusps).

Hypotheses and conventions:

- Γ″ acts freely on ℍ, so X = X(Γ″) is a compact Riemann surface with no elliptic points and the weight-k forms form a holomorphic line bundle L_k on X (holomorphic at the cusps); D = sum of the cusps.

Source support:

- [bruinier-funke-2004](#reference-bruinier-funke-2004), Thm. 3.7, p. 13. The statement, here for Γ″.
- [bruinier-funke-2004](#reference-bruinier-funke-2004), proof of Thm. 3.7, p. 14. The Serre duality step.
- [bruinier-funke-2004](#reference-bruinier-funke-2004), proof of Thm. 3.7, p. 14. The vanishing step.

Direct prerequisites: [QM.3/local-xi-preimage-at-cusps](#QM-3-local-xi-preimage-at-cusps), [QM.3/xi-map](#QM-3-xi-map), [QM.3/xi-holomorphic-iff-harmonic](#QM-3-xi-holomorphic-iff-harmonic), [QM.3/harmonic-maass-form](#QM-3-harmonic-maass-form), [QM.3/weakly-holomorphic-modular-form](#QM-3-weakly-holomorphic-modular-form).

Construction or proof route:

1. Let g ∈ M^!_{2−k}(Γ″). For each cusp c = σ_c∞ take F_c := F_{σ_c}∘σ_c^{−1} slashed back (QM.3/local-xi-preimage-at-cusps) and a smooth cut-off χ_c on X equal to 1 near c and supported in a small punctured disc; f₀ := Σ_c χ_c F_c is a smooth weight-k function on ℍ with ξ_k f₀ = g near every cusp.
2. The (0,1)-form ω := (i/2)v^{−k}\overline{(g − ξ_k f₀)}dτ̄ is a smooth section of E^{0,1}(X, L_k) with compact support in X minus the cusps.
3. Dolbeault: H¹(X, L_k ⊗ O_{nD}) ≅ E^{0,1}(X, L_k ⊗ O_{nD})/∂̄E^{0,0}(X, L_k ⊗ O_{nD}) (upstream: Tau Ceti ModularForms 10B, Dolbeault resolution of an invertible sheaf).
4. Serre duality with the cusp twist K_X ≅ L_2(−D): H¹(X, L_k ⊗ O_{nD}) ≅ H⁰(X, L_{2−k} ⊗ O_{−(n+1)D})^*, which is 0 for n large because a non-zero form of weight 2 − k has a bounded number of zeros (valence bound) (upstream: Tau Ceti ModularForms 10B (iv) for invertible sheaves, 10C automorphy line bundles).
5. So ω = ∂̄f₁ with f₁ a smooth section of L_k ⊗ O_{nD}, i.e. a smooth weight-k Γ″-invariant function with exponential growth at the cusps and ∂_τ̄f₁ = (i/2)v^{−k}\overline{(g − ξ_kf₀)}.
6. f := f₀ + f₁ satisfies ξ_k f = 2iv^k\overline{∂̄f} = ξ_kf₀ + (g − ξ_kf₀) = g, which is holomorphic, so Δ_k f = 0 (QM.3/xi-holomorphic-iff-harmonic): f ∈ H_k(Γ″).

Acceptance checks:

- For Γ″ = Γ(3), k = 2, g = 3/π this produces E₂* up to M^!_2(Γ(3)).

<a id="QM-3-xi-surjective-descent"></a>

### Descent of ξ-preimages along a normal subgroup

**Lemma** (`QM.3/xi-surjective-descent`). Let Γ″ ⊴ Γ be arithmetic subgroups with finite index [Γ : Γ″], k ∈ ℤ, and g ∈ M^!_{2−k}(Γ). If f″ ∈ H_k(Γ″) satisfies ξ_k f″ = g, then f := [Γ : Γ″]^{−1}Σ_{γ ∈ Γ″\Γ} f″|_kγ lies in H_k(Γ) and ξ_k f = g.

Hypotheses and conventions:

- Γ″ normal in Γ, of finite index; Γ.HasDetOne.

Source support:

- [bruinier-funke-2004](#reference-bruinier-funke-2004), proof of Thm. 3.7, p. 15. The descent step, realised by averaging.

Direct prerequisites: [QM.3/harmonic-maass-form](#QM-3-harmonic-maass-form), [QM.3/xi-slash-equivariance](#QM-3-xi-slash-equivariance), [QM.3/laplacian-slash-equivariance](#QM-3-laplacian-slash-equivariance), [QM.3/xi-map](#QM-3-xi-map).

Construction or proof route:

1. Γ″ normal ⇒ f″|_kγ ∈ H_k(Γ″) for γ ∈ Γ (slash-invariance under γ^{−1}Γ″γ = Γ″, Δ_k equivariance, growth at the permuted cusps), and the sum over Γ″\Γ is well defined and Γ-invariant.
2. ξ_k(f″|_kγ) = (ξ_kf″)|_{2−k}γ = g|_{2−k}γ = g (QM.3/xi-slash-equivariance and Γ-invariance of g), so ξ_k f = g.

Acceptance checks:

- This is BF's 'cohomology of a finite group acting on a ℂ-vector space vanishes', made explicit as averaging.

<a id="QM-3-xi-surjective"></a>

### Surjectivity of ξ_k (Bruinier–Funke Theorem 3.7)

**Theorem** (`QM.3/xi-surjective`). Let Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) have finite index and k ∈ ℤ, k ≠ 1. Then ξ_k : H_k(Γ) → M^!_{2−k}(Γ) is surjective.

Hypotheses and conventions:

- Finite index in SL₂(ℤ); k ≠ 1.

Source support:

- [bruinier-funke-2004](#reference-bruinier-funke-2004), Thm. 3.7, p. 13. Exactly the statement (scalar case, finite-index Γ as allowed by BF p. 12).

Direct prerequisites: [QM.3/normal-torsion-free-subgroup](#QM-3-normal-torsion-free-subgroup), [QM.3/xi-surjective-free-normal](#QM-3-xi-surjective-free-normal), [QM.3/xi-surjective-descent](#QM-3-xi-surjective-descent).

Construction or proof route:

1. Choose Γ″ ≤ Γ normal in SL₂(ℤ), of finite index, acting freely on ℍ (QM.3/normal-torsion-free-subgroup); Γ″ is normal in Γ.
2. g ∈ M^!_{2−k}(Γ) ⊆ M^!_{2−k}(Γ″); take f″ ∈ H_k(Γ″) with ξ_kf″ = g (QM.3/xi-surjective-free-normal).
3. Average over Γ″\Γ (QM.3/xi-surjective-descent).

Acceptance checks:

- k = 2, Γ = SL₂(ℤ), g = 3/π: a preimage is E₂*.
- k ≥ 2 with 2 − k < 0: every weakly holomorphic form of negative weight 2 − k is a ξ-image (e.g. of harmonic forms built from Poincaré series).

<a id="QM-3-bruinier-funke-exact-sequences"></a>

### The exact sequences 0 → M^!_k → H_k → M^!_{2−k} → 0 and 0 → M^!_k → H_k^+ → S_{2−k} → 0

**Theorem** (`QM.3/bruinier-funke-exact-sequences`). For Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) of finite index and k ∈ ℤ, k ≠ 1, the sequences 0 → M^!_k(Γ) → H_k(Γ) → M^!_{2−k}(Γ) → 0 and 0 → M^!_k(Γ) → H_k^+(Γ) → S_{2−k}(Γ) → 0 (the second map is ξ_k) are exact (Bruinier–Funke Cor. 3.8).

Hypotheses and conventions:

- As in QM.3/xi-surjective. The maps are ℂ-linear (inclusion) and conjugate-linear (ξ_k); exactness is as sets/additive groups.

Source support:

- [bruinier-funke-2004](#reference-bruinier-funke-2004), Cor. 3.8, p. 15. Exactly the statement (ξ_k on the arrows).

Direct prerequisites: [QM.3/xi-surjective](#QM-3-xi-surjective), [QM.3/xi-kernel-weakly-holomorphic](#QM-3-xi-kernel-weakly-holomorphic), [QM.3/harmonic-maass-form-plus-space](#QM-3-harmonic-maass-form-plus-space).

Construction or proof route:

1. Injectivity of M^!_k → H_k: toHarmonic is injective.
2. Exactness in the middle: QM.3/xi-kernel-weakly-holomorphic.
3. Surjectivity of the first sequence: QM.3/xi-surjective.
4. Second sequence: for h ∈ S_{2−k}(Γ) ⊆ M^!_{2−k}(Γ) any ξ-preimage lies in H_k^+ by definition; kernel as before.

Acceptance checks:

- k = 2, Γ = SL₂(ℤ): ξ_2 maps H_2 onto M^!_0 with E₂* ↦ 3/π, and H_2^+ = M^!_2 since S_0 = 0.
- k ≤ 0 even, level one: dim H_k^+/M^!_k = dim S_{2−k}(SL₂(ℤ)), e.g. 1 for k = −10.

<a id="QM-3-bruinier-funke-duality"></a>

### Non-degeneracy of {·,·} on H_k^+/M^!_k × S_{2−k} (Bruinier–Funke Theorem 3.6)

**Theorem** (`QM.3/bruinier-funke-duality`). For Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) of finite index and k ∈ ℤ, k ≠ 1: (a) if g ∈ S_{2−k}(Γ) and {g, f} = 0 for all f ∈ H_k^+(Γ) then g = 0; (b) if f ∈ H_k^+(Γ) and {g, f} = 0 for all g ∈ S_{2−k}(Γ) then f ∈ M^!_k(Γ). Hence {·,·} induces a perfect pairing between H_k^+(Γ)/M^!_k(Γ) and S_{2−k}(Γ) (finite-dimensional).

Hypotheses and conventions:

- As before.

Source support:

- [bruinier-funke-2004](#reference-bruinier-funke-2004), Thm. 3.6, p. 13. Exactly the statement and the reduction.

Direct prerequisites: [QM.3/bruinier-funke-pairing](#QM-3-bruinier-funke-pairing), [QM.3/xi-surjective](#QM-3-xi-surjective), [QM.3/xi-kernel-weakly-holomorphic](#QM-3-xi-kernel-weakly-holomorphic), `tauceti:CuspForm.peterssonInnerCosets_definite`.

Construction or proof route:

1. (a) By QM.3/xi-surjective choose f ∈ H_k^+ with ξ_kf = g; then 0 = {g, f} = (g, g) forces g = 0 (Tau Ceti CuspForm.peterssonInnerCosets_definite).
2. (b) Take g = ξ_kf ∈ S_{2−k}: (ξ_kf, ξ_kf) = 0 gives ξ_kf = 0, so f ∈ M^!_k (QM.3/xi-kernel-weakly-holomorphic).

Acceptance checks:

- Level one, k = −10: S_{12} = ℂΔ and H_{−10}^+/M^!_{−10} is spanned by Q(−1, 12, 1) with {Δ, Q(−1, 12, 1)} = τ(1) = 1.

<a id="QM-3-bruinier-funke-negative-pairing"></a>

### The pairing {g, f}′ over negative indices

**Definition** (`QM.3/bruinier-funke-negative-pairing`). For Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) of finite index, k ∈ ℤ, k ≠ 1, g ∈ M_{2−k}(Γ) and f ∈ H_k^+(Γ): {g, f}′ := Σ_{c ∈ Γ\ℙ¹(ℚ)} w_c Σ_{n<0} a⁺_c(n)b_c(−n) (notation of QM.3/bruinier-funke-pairing-formula); for Γ = SL₂(ℤ), {g, f}′ = Σ_{n<0}a⁺(n)b(−n) (Bruinier–Funke (3.15)). It differs from {g, f} by the constant-term contribution Σ_c w_c a⁺_c(0)b_c(0).

Hypotheses and conventions:

- Same data as the pairing formula.
- Fourier coefficients use the strict period h_c. Cusp-sum weights are w_c := widthInfty(σ_c^{−1}Γσ_c), the orbit length for Γ·{±I}; w_c = h_c at regular cusps and w_c = h_c/2 at irregular cusps.

Source support:

- [bruinier-funke-2004](#reference-bruinier-funke-2004), (3.15), p. 15. Exactly the definition (level one); the cusp-weighted form for finite index.

Direct prerequisites: [QM.3/bruinier-funke-pairing-formula](#QM-3-bruinier-funke-pairing-formula), [QM.3/holomorphic-part](#QM-3-holomorphic-part).

Construction or proof route:

1. Finite sums: a⁺_c(n) = 0 for n ≪ 0.
2. {g, f} − {g, f}′ = Σ_c w_c a⁺_c(0)b_c(0) by QM.3/bruinier-funke-pairing-formula.
3. If g ∈ S_{2−k} (all b_c(0) = 0) then {g, f}′ = {g, f}.

Uses that determine the API:

- Bruinier–Funke Cor. 3.9: non-degeneracy on H^+/M^!! × M_κ
- Bruinier–Funke Prop. 3.11: the functional λ_Q(g) = {g, h}′ represented by h ∈ H^+

Named declarations and API:

- `bruinierFunkePairing'` (data): {g, f}′ = Σ_c w_c Σ_{n<0} a⁺_c(n)b_c(−n).
- `bruinierFunkePairing'_eq_of_isCuspForm` (compatibility): {g, f}′ = {g, f} for g ∈ S_{2−k}(Γ).
- `bruinierFunkePairing_sub_bruinierFunkePairing'` (relation): {g, f} − {g, f}′ = Σ_c w_c a⁺_c(0)b_c(0).

Unit tests:

- `bruinierFunkePairing'_cuspForm_test` (compatibility): For g a cusp form, {g, f}′ = {g, f}.
- `bruinierFunkePairing'_const_test` (computation): Level one, f ∈ M^!_k(SL₂(ℤ)) with principal part a(−1)q^{−1} + a(0), g ∈ M_{2−k}: {g, f}′ = a(−1)b(1).
- `bruinierFunkePairing'_ne_test` (non-example): Level one, k = −10, g = E₁₂, f = Q(−1, 12, 1): {g, f} = 0 but {g, f}′ = b_{E₁₂}(1) = 65520/691 ≠ 0.

Acceptance checks:

- {g, f}′ = {g, f} for cusp forms g; for f = E₂* ∉ H^+ the pairing is not defined.

<a id="QM-3-weakly-holomorphic-constant-term-orthogonal"></a>

### The subspace M^!!_k(Γ)

**Definition** (`QM.3/weakly-holomorphic-constant-term-orthogonal`). For Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) of finite index and k ∈ ℤ: M^!!_k(Γ) := {f ∈ M^!_k(Γ) : Σ_c w_c a_c(0)b_c(0) = 0 for every g ∈ M_{2−k}(Γ)}, the weakly holomorphic forms whose constant terms are orthogonal to the constant terms of all holomorphic modular forms of weight 2 − k (Bruinier–Funke p. 15, scalar case). For f ∈ M^!!_k or g ∈ S_{2−k}: {g, f} = {g, f}′.

Hypotheses and conventions:

- Finite-index Γ.
- Fourier coefficients use the strict period h_c. Cusp-sum weights are w_c := widthInfty(σ_c^{−1}Γσ_c), the orbit length for Γ·{±I}; w_c = h_c at regular cusps and w_c = h_c/2 at irregular cusps.

Source support:

- [bruinier-funke-2004](#reference-bruinier-funke-2004), p. 15. Exactly the definition (scalar case, cusp-weighted for finite index).
- [bruinier-funke-2004](#reference-bruinier-funke-2004), p. 15. The simplification for k < 0.

Direct prerequisites: [QM.3/weakly-holomorphic-modular-form](#QM-3-weakly-holomorphic-modular-form), [QM.3/weakly-holomorphic-laurent-expansion](#QM-3-weakly-holomorphic-laurent-expansion), `mathlib:ModularForm`, `mathlib:ModularForm.E`.

Construction or proof route:

1. A submodule: the condition is linear in f.
2. If M_{2−k}(Γ) realises every tuple of constant terms at the cusps (Eisenstein series of weight 2 − k ≥ 3), M^!!_k(Γ) is the space of f with vanishing constant terms at all cusps (BF p. 15); at level one this holds for every even k < 0, and M^!!_0 = M^!_0 because M_2(SL₂(ℤ)) = 0.

Uses that determine the API:

- Bruinier–Funke Cor. 3.9: the quotient H^+/M^!! pairs perfectly with M_κ

Named declarations and API:

- `weaklyHolomorphicPerp` (data): The submodule M^!!_k(Γ) of M^!_k(Γ).
- `mem_weaklyHolomorphicPerp_iff` (characterisation): f ∈ M^!! ↔ ∀ g ∈ M_{2−k}(Γ), Σ_c w_c a_c(0)b_c(0) = 0.
- `weaklyHolomorphicPerp_eq_of_neg` (other): Level one, k < 0: M^!!_k = {f : a(0) = 0}.

Unit tests:

- `mem_weaklyHolomorphicPerp_j_test` (computation): j = E₄³/Δ ∈ M^!!_0(SL₂(ℤ)) (M_2(SL₂(ℤ)) = 0) although its constant term is 744.
- `not_mem_weaklyHolomorphicPerp_test` (non-example): E₄/Δ ∈ M^!_{−8}(SL₂(ℤ)) has constant term 264 ≠ 0 (E₄/Δ = q^{−1} + 264 + O(q)), so it is not in M^!!_{−8}.
- `weaklyHolomorphicPerp_le_test` (degenerate): M^!!_k(Γ) ≤ M^!_k(Γ); for k ≥ 3, M_{2−k}(Γ) = 0 and M^!!_k = M^!_k.

Acceptance checks:

- Level one, k < 0 even: M^!!_k = {f ∈ M^!_k : a(0) = 0} (E_{2−k} has constant term 1).
- Level one, k = 0: M^!!_0 = M^!_0 since M_2(SL₂(ℤ)) = 0 (e.g. j ∈ M^!!_0 although a(0) = 744).

<a id="QM-3-principal-part-residue-pairing"></a>

### Spaces of principal parts and the residue pairing

**Definition** (`QM.3/principal-part-residue-pairing`). For Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) of finite index with cusp classes c (representatives σ_c, widths h_c): Sing_k(Γ) := the subspace of ⊕_c ℂ[q_c^{−1}] consisting of Laurent polynomials in q_c = e(τ/h_c) with non-positive exponents whose Fourier polynomials are invariant under the weight-k slash action of each cusp stabilizer (including constant terms), PowSer(Γ) := ⊕_c ℂ[[q_c]], and the residue pairing of weight-(2−k) expansions with weight-k principal parts ⟨F, P⟩ := Σ_c w_c Σ_{n≥0} F_c(n)P_c(−n) = Σ_c w_c Res_{q_c=0}(F_cP_c q_c^{−1}dq_c) (Borcherds, GKZ §3, scalar case). The maps λ : M^!_k(Γ) → Sing_k(Γ) (principal parts with constant terms at all cusps) and λ : M_{2−k}(Γ) → PowSer(Γ) (expansions at all cusps).

Hypotheses and conventions:

- Scalar integral weight, with local stabilizer compatibility retained. If −I ∈ Γ and k is odd, Sing_k(Γ) = 0. At an irregular cusp with h_c = 2w_c, only exponents n ≡ k (mod 2) are allowed. The geometric residue coefficient is w_c/(2πi), since products of the two weights descend with period w_c.
- Fourier coefficients use the strict period h_c. Cusp-sum weights are w_c := widthInfty(σ_c^{−1}Γσ_c), the orbit length for Γ·{±I}; w_c = h_c at regular cusps and w_c = h_c/2 at irregular cusps.

Source support:

- [borcherds-gkz-1999](#reference-borcherds-gkz-1999), §3, p. 4. The residue pairing at one cusp.
- [borcherds-gkz-1999](#reference-borcherds-gkz-1999), §3, p. 5. The spaces and the map λ.

Direct prerequisites: [QM.3/weakly-holomorphic-laurent-expansion](#QM-3-weakly-holomorphic-laurent-expansion), `mathlib:LaurentPolynomial`, `mathlib:UpperHalfPlane.qExpansion`, `mathlib:Subgroup.widthInfty`.

Construction or proof route:

1. Define the finite cusp-indexed families and their subspace of non-positive Laurent polynomials. Impose IsCompatiblePrincipalPart Γ k P: for every cusp c, its Fourier polynomial is fixed by the weight-k slash action of the stabilizer of ∞ in σ_c^{−1}Γσ_c. Closure is linear. Use h_c for its Fourier exponents and w_c for the residue/orbit weight.
2. The pairing is well defined (finite sums) and independent of the representatives σ_c up to the common translation.

Uses that determine the API:

- Borcherds GKZ Thm. 3.1: λ(M^!_k) = λ(M_{2−k})^⊥
- Bruinier–Funke Prop. 3.11: existence of weakly holomorphic forms with prescribed principal parts

Named declarations and API:

- `PrincipalPartSpace` (data): Sing_k(Γ): the weight-k cusp-stabilizer-compatible submodule of non-positive Laurent-polynomial families.
- `residuePairing` (data): ⟨F, P⟩ = Σ_c w_c Σ_{n≥0}F_c(n)P_c(−n).
- `principalPartMap` (data): λ : M^!_k(Γ) → Sing_k(Γ); expansions satisfy the stabilizer law.
- `residuePairing_principalPartMap_eq_zero` (relation): ⟨λ(g), λ(f)⟩ = 0 for f ∈ M^!_k(Γ), g ∈ M_{2−k}(Γ).
- `IsCompatiblePrincipalPart` (characterisation): Each Fourier polynomial is fixed by the weight-k slash action of its full cusp stabilizer; −I forces zero in odd weight and −T^{w_c} forces n ≡ k mod 2 at an irregular cusp.
- `cuspOrbitWidth` (compatibility): w_c is Mathlib Subgroup.widthInfty of σ_c^{−1}Γσ_c; h_c remains its strictWidthInfty.

Unit tests:

- `residuePairing_levelOne_test` (computation): Level one: ⟨λ(E₄), T^{−1} + c⟩ = 240 + c.
- `residuePairing_weaklyHolomorphic_test` (characterisation): For f ∈ M^!_k(Γ), g ∈ M_{2−k}(Γ): ⟨λ(g), λ(f)⟩ = 0 (residue theorem on X(Γ)).
- `residuePairing_zero_test` (degenerate): ⟨F, 0⟩ = 0 and ⟨0, P⟩ = 0.
- `principalPartSpace_odd_levelOne_test` (non-example): For odd k at level one, q^{−1} is not an admissible principal part, since −I acts by −1.
- `principalPartSpace_irregular_test` (non-example): At ∞ for the preimage of ⟨−T mod 4⟩, h=2 and w=1. In even weight q_2^{−1} is inadmissible while q_2^{−2} is admissible; a raw non-positive-polynomial space misses this restriction.

Acceptance checks:

- Level one: ⟨λ(E₄), T^{−1} + c⟩ = b(1) + c·b(0) = 240 + c.

<a id="QM-3-borcherds-obstruction-theorem"></a>

### Borcherds' obstruction theorem (Serre duality for principal parts)

**Theorem** (`QM.3/borcherds-obstruction-theorem`). Let Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) have finite index and k ∈ ℤ. A principal part P ∈ Sing_k(Γ) is the principal part (with constant terms) of some f ∈ M^!_k(Γ) if and only if ⟨λ(g), P⟩ = 0 for every g ∈ M_{2−k}(Γ). Equivalently λ(M^!_k(Γ)) = λ(M_{2−k}(Γ))^⊥ and the obstruction space Sing_k(Γ)/λ(M^!_k(Γ)) is dual to M_{2−k}(Γ) (Borcherds, GKZ Theorem 3.1, scalar case with Borcherds' k replaced by 2 − k).

Hypotheses and conventions:

- Scalar case; Γ of finite index in SL₂(ℤ).
- Fourier coefficients use the strict period h_c. Cusp-sum weights are w_c := widthInfty(σ_c^{−1}Γσ_c), the orbit length for Γ·{±I}; w_c = h_c at regular cusps and w_c = h_c/2 at irregular cusps.
- P is cusp-stabilizer-compatible in weight k as defined in QM.3/principal-part-residue-pairing; arbitrary raw Laurent families are not allowed.

Source support:

- [borcherds-gkz-1999](#reference-borcherds-gkz-1999), Thm. 3.1, p. 5. Theorem 3.1 includes the stabilizer-character compatibility omitted by the original scalar extraction; the theorem conclusion follows in the next sentence. Weight-k principal-part compatibility is retained here.
- [borcherds-gkz-1999](#reference-borcherds-gkz-1999), proof of Thm. 3.1, p. 5. The Serre-duality step.

Direct prerequisites: [QM.3/principal-part-residue-pairing](#QM-3-principal-part-residue-pairing), [QM.3/normal-torsion-free-subgroup](#QM-3-normal-torsion-free-subgroup), [QM.3/weakly-holomorphic-modular-form](#QM-3-weakly-holomorphic-modular-form).

Construction or proof route:

1. Necessity: QM.3/principal-part-residue-pairing (residue theorem for the meromorphic differential f g dτ on X(Γ)).
2. Sufficiency for Γ″ acting freely: identify H⁰(L_{2−k}) with M_{2−k}, the obstruction space with H¹(X, L_k ⊗ L_cusp^∗) (Mittag-Leffler for sections with prescribed singularities at the cusps), and apply Serre duality H¹(L_k ⊗ L_cusp^∗)^∗ ≅ H⁰(Ω ⊗ L_cusp ⊗ L_{−k}) = H⁰(L_{2−k}) (Ω ≅ L_2 ⊗ L_cusp^∗), the pairing being the sum of residues (upstream: Tau Ceti ModularForms 10B (iv), 10C).
3. General Γ: pass to Γ″ ⊴ Γ (QM.3/normal-torsion-free-subgroup) and take Γ/Γ″-invariants of a perfect Γ/Γ″-equivariant duality (complete reducibility of finite-group representations over ℂ).

Acceptance checks:

- Level one, k = 0: T^{−1} + c is realised (by j + c − 744) for every c since M_2(SL₂(ℤ)) = 0.
- Level one, k = −10: T^{−1} + c is realised iff ⟨λ(E₁₂), T^{−1} + c⟩ = 65520/691 + c = 0 and ⟨λ(Δ), ·⟩ = 1 = 0 — never; so no weakly holomorphic form of weight −10 has principal part q^{−1} + c (the obstruction is Δ).

<a id="QM-3-bruinier-funke-duality-negative"></a>

### Non-degeneracy of {·,·}′ (Bruinier–Funke Corollary 3.9)

**Theorem** (`QM.3/bruinier-funke-duality-negative`). For Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) of finite index and k ∈ ℤ, k ≠ 1, k ≠ 2, the pairing {·,·}′ induces non-degenerate pairings between H_k^+(Γ)/M^!!_k(Γ) and M_{2−k}(Γ), and between H_k^+(Γ)/M^!_k(Γ) and S_{2−k}(Γ).

Hypotheses and conventions:

- As before.
- Fourier coefficients use the strict period h_c. Cusp-sum weights are w_c := widthInfty(σ_c^{−1}Γσ_c), the orbit length for Γ·{±I}; w_c = h_c at regular cusps and w_c = h_c/2 at irregular cusps.
- Exclude k=2: for scalar level one, g=1 ∈ M_0 is nonzero but has b(n)=0 for all n>0, so {1,f}′=0 for every f. The source Corollary 3.9 is false in this case (E409). The ordinary cusp-form pairing remains non-degenerate at k=2.

Source support:

- [bruinier-funke-2004](#reference-bruinier-funke-2004), Cor. 3.9, p. 15. The source claim requires excluding scalar k=2; E409 records a counterexample. The proof below applies when 2−k≠0.

Direct prerequisites: [QM.3/bruinier-funke-negative-pairing](#QM-3-bruinier-funke-negative-pairing), [QM.3/weakly-holomorphic-constant-term-orthogonal](#QM-3-weakly-holomorphic-constant-term-orthogonal), [QM.3/bruinier-funke-duality](#QM-3-bruinier-funke-duality), [QM.3/borcherds-obstruction-theorem](#QM-3-borcherds-obstruction-theorem).

Construction or proof route:

1. Second pairing: {g, f}′ = {g, f} for g ∈ S_{2−k}, so this is QM.3/bruinier-funke-duality.
2. {g, f}′ = 0 for f ∈ M^!!_k: {g, f} = 0 (f ∈ M^!) and the constant-term correction vanishes by definition of M^!!.
3. Left kernel: let g ∈ M_{2−k} with {g, f}′ = 0 for all f ∈ H_k^+. If g ∈ S_{2−k}, g = 0 by QM.3/bruinier-funke-duality. Otherwise some b_c(0) ≠ 0; by QM.3/borcherds-obstruction-theorem the realisable principal parts are λ(M_{2−k})^⊥, and if the functional P ↦ Σ_c w_c P_c(0)b_c(0) vanished on λ(M_{2−k})^⊥ it would lie in the finite-dimensional λ(M_{2−k}), giving g′ ∈ M_{2−k} with all non-constant coefficients 0, hence constant, hence 0 for 2 − k ≠ 0 — contradiction; so some f ∈ M^!_k has {g, f}′ = −Σ w_c a_c(0)b_c(0) ≠ 0.
4. Right kernel: f ∈ H_k^+ with {g, f}′ = 0 ∀ g ∈ M_{2−k}: then f ∈ M^!_k (take g cusp forms and QM.3/bruinier-funke-duality), and then the constant-term condition says f ∈ M^!!_k.

Acceptance checks:

- Level one, k = −10: E₁₂ pairs non-trivially with Q(−1, 12, 1) under {·,·}′ (value 65520/691).

<a id="QM-3-harmonic-maass-form-prescribed-principal-parts"></a>

### Harmonic Maass forms with prescribed principal parts (Bruinier–Funke Prop. 3.11)

**Theorem** (`QM.3/harmonic-maass-form-prescribed-principal-parts`). Let Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) have finite index, k ∈ ℤ, k ≠ 1. For every cusp-stabilizer-compatible family (Q_c)_c in Sing_k(Γ) of Laurent polynomials in q_c^{−1} with only negative exponents, one per cusp class c, there is f ∈ H_k^+(Γ) whose principal part at every cusp c is Q_c + (a constant). If k < 0, f is unique (M_k(Γ) = 0 and constant principal parts force f ∈ M_k). For Γ = SL₂(ℤ) this is Bruinier–Funke Prop. 3.11; the all-cusps form is the one used in Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades' proof of Corollary 4.3 ('According to Lemma 3.11 of [7]').

Hypotheses and conventions:

- k ≠ 1; for uniqueness k < 0.
- Fourier coefficients use the strict period h_c. Cusp-sum weights are w_c := widthInfty(σ_c^{−1}Γσ_c), the orbit length for Γ·{±I}; w_c = h_c at regular cusps and w_c = h_c/2 at irregular cusps.
- Require the same cusp-stabilizer compatibility as Sing_k(Γ). If −I ∈ Γ and k is odd, only Q=0 is possible; raw arbitrary coefficients cannot be prescribed.

Source support:

- [bruinier-funke-2004](#reference-bruinier-funke-2004), Prop. 3.11, p. 16. Prescribed principal parts must respect the full stabilizer law (including the central element); the source preceding paragraph symmetrises h and −h. The scalar extraction now imposes this compatibility explicitly.
- [bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008](#reference-bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008), proof of Cor. 4.3, p. 10. The all-cusps form used for finite-index Γ.

Direct prerequisites: [QM.3/bruinier-funke-duality](#QM-3-bruinier-funke-duality), [QM.3/borcherds-obstruction-theorem](#QM-3-borcherds-obstruction-theorem), [QM.3/principal-part](#QM-3-principal-part), [QM.3/plus-space-principal-part-characterisation](#QM-3-plus-space-principal-part-characterisation).

Construction or proof route:

1. λ_Q(g) := Σ_c w_c Σ_{n<0} Q_c(n)b_c(−n) is a linear functional on S_{2−k}(Γ); by QM.3/bruinier-funke-duality there is h ∈ H_k^+ with {g, h} = {g, h}′ = λ_Q(g) (g cusp) for all g ∈ S_{2−k}.
2. Then λ_{Q − P(h)} vanishes on S_{2−k}; choose constants c_c so that the principal part Q − P(h) + c is orthogonal to λ(M_{2−k}) (the Eisenstein part of M_{2−k} is detected by constant terms), and apply QM.3/borcherds-obstruction-theorem to get h′ ∈ M^!_k with that principal part.
3. f := h + h′.
4. Uniqueness for k < 0: two solutions differ by f₀ ∈ H_k^+ with constant principal parts; {g, f₀} = Σ w_c a_c(0)b_c(0) = 0 for cusp forms, so ξf₀ = 0 and f₀ ∈ M^!_k with constant principal parts, i.e. f₀ ∈ M_k(Γ) = 0.

Acceptance checks:

- Level one, k = 2 − κ with κ ≥ 4 even: the unique f with principal part q^{−m} + const is Q(−m, κ, 1) (QM.3/level-one-plus-space-spanned-by-poincare-series).

<a id="QM-3-classical-kloosterman-sum"></a>

### The classical Kloosterman sum K(m, n, c)

**Definition** (`QM.3/classical-kloosterman-sum`). For m, n ∈ ℤ and c ∈ ℕ, c ≥ 1: K(m, n, c) := Σ_{v ∈ (ℤ/cℤ)^×} e((m v̄ + n v)/c), where v v̄ ≡ 1 mod c (Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades (6.6)). This is the untwisted Kloosterman sum; it is not the eta-multiplier sum A_k(n) of Rademacher's formula (QM.2/kloosterman-sum-rademacher).

Hypotheses and conventions:

- c ≥ 1; for c = 1 the sum has the single term v = 0 ∈ (ℤ/1)^× and K(m, n, 1) = 1.

Source support:

- [bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008](#reference-bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008), (6.6), p. 15. Exactly the definition.

Direct prerequisites: `mathlib:ZMod`.

Construction or proof route:

1. Define as a finite sum over the units of ZMod c with the additive character e(·/c).
2. Symmetry K(m, n, c) = K(n, m, c) (substitute v ↦ v̄) and K(m, n, c) = K(−m, −n, c) = \overline{K(m, n, c)} (substitute v ↦ −v), so K is real.
3. K(m, 0, c) = K(0, m, c) is the Ramanujan sum c_c(m); K(0, 0, c) = φ(c).

Uses that determine the API:

- Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades Prop. 6.1, 6.2: Fourier coefficients of holomorphic and Maass–Poincaré series
- Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades Prop. 6.2: b(−m, k, N; 0) involves K(−m, 0, c), a Ramanujan sum

Named declarations and API:

- `kloostermanSum` (data): K(m, n, c) = Σ_{v ∈ (ZMod c)ˣ} e((m v⁻¹ + n v)/c).
- `kloostermanSum_comm` (relation): K(m, n, c) = K(n, m, c).
- `kloostermanSum_neg` (relation): K(−m, −n, c) = K(m, n, c) = conj K(m, n, c).
- `kloostermanSum_zero_right` (example): K(m, 0, c) = Σ_{v ∈ (ZMod c)ˣ} e(mv/c) (Ramanujan's sum), in particular K(0, 0, c) = φ(c).
- `kloostermanSum_one` (simp): K(m, n, 1) = 1.

Unit tests:

- `kloostermanSum_one_one_three_test` (computation): K(1, 1, 3) = −1.
- `kloostermanSum_zero_zero_test` (degenerate): K(0, 0, c) = φ(c) (Euler's totient) for c ≥ 1.
- `kloostermanSum_one_one_five_test` (non-example): K(1, 1, 5) = 2 + 2cos(4π/5) ≠ −1 = Σ_{v ∈ (ℤ/5)^×} e(2v/5): the inverse v̄ matters.
- `kloostermanSum_conj_test` (characterisation): conj K(m, n, c) = K(m, n, c) (K is real).

Acceptance checks:

- K(1, 1, 3) = −1; K(1, 1, 5) = 2 + 2cos(4π/5); K(0, 0, c) = φ(c).

<a id="QM-3-holomorphic-poincare-series"></a>

### Holomorphic Poincaré series P(m, k, N)

**Definition** (`QM.3/holomorphic-poincare-series`). For N ≥ 1, an even integer k ≥ 4 and m ∈ ℤ: P(m, k, N; τ) := Σ_{A ∈ Γ∞\Γ₀(N)} (e(mτ)|_kA)(τ), Γ∞ = {±T^n}, i.e. Σ over coprime (c, d) with N | c modulo ±1 of (cτ + d)^{−k}e(m(aτ + b)/(cτ + d)) (Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades (6.4), (6.5) with φ_m(y) = e(imy) = e^{−2πmy}). The series converges absolutely and locally uniformly for k ≥ 3 when m ≥ 0 and for all m (poles are only at the cusps) because |e(mAτ)| ≤ e^{2π|m|Im Aτ} and Im Aτ ≤ 1/(c²v) for c ≠ 0.

Hypotheses and conventions:

- k even (for odd k the terms for ±A cancel), k ≥ 4 (absolute convergence; BOR treat k = 2 by analytic continuation, not planned here).
- Normalisation: the identity coset contributes e(mτ).

Source support:

- [bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008](#reference-bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008), (6.4), (6.5), pp. 14–15. Exactly the definition.
- [bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008](#reference-bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008), Prop. 6.1, p. 15. API items (membership).

Direct prerequisites: [QM.3/weakly-holomorphic-modular-form](#QM-3-weakly-holomorphic-modular-form), `mathlib:CongruenceSubgroup.Gamma0`, `mathlib:EisensteinSeries.summable_norm_eisSummand`, `mathlib:EisensteinSeries.eisensteinSeries_tendstoLocallyUniformly`, `mathlib:ModularForm.E`, `mathlib:CuspForm`.

Construction or proof route:

1. Well defined on Γ∞\Γ₀(N): e(mτ)|_kT^n = e(mτ), and |_k(−I) = (−1)^k = 1.
2. Convergence: Σ_{(c,d)}|cτ + d|^{−k} converges locally uniformly for k ≥ 3 (Mathlib's EisensteinSeries.summable_norm_eisSummand / eisensteinSeries_tendstoLocallyUniformly), and e^{2π|m|/(c²v)} is bounded for c ≠ 0 on compacta.
3. Holomorphic (locally uniform limit), Γ₀(N)-invariant of weight k (re-indexing the sum).
4. Growth: at ∞ the identity term gives e(mτ); all other terms are O(v^{1−k}) in total; similarly at other cusps. Hence P(m) ∈ M^!_k(Γ₀(N)), a cusp form for m ≥ 1, and P(0, k, 1) = ModularForm.E k.

Uses that determine the API:

- Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades §6.2: ξ_{2−k}Q(−m, k, N) = (4πm)^{k−1}/(k−2)!·P(m, k, N) and D^{k−1}Q(−m, k, N) = −m^{k−1}P(−m, k, N)
- Bruinier–Funke Remark 3.10: ξ-images of Maass–Poincaré series are holomorphic Poincaré series, which span the cusp forms
- QM.3/level-one-cusp-forms-spanned-by-poincare-series: spanning S_k(SL₂(ℤ))

Named declarations and API:

- `holomorphicPoincareSeries` (data): P(m, k, N; τ) = Σ_{A ∈ Γ∞\Γ₀(N)} (e(mτ)|_kA)(τ).
- `holomorphicPoincareSeries_summable` (other): The defining series converges absolutely, locally uniformly on ℍ (k ≥ 4 even).
- `holomorphicPoincareSeries_slash` (structure): P(m, k, N)|_kγ = P(m, k, N) for γ ∈ Γ₀(N).
- `holomorphicPoincareSeries_toCuspForm` (constructor): For m ≥ 1, P(m, k, N) as an element of S_k(Γ₀(N)).
- `holomorphicPoincareSeries_toWeaklyHolomorphic` (constructor): For all m, P(m, k, N) as an element of M^!_k(Γ₀(N)).
- `holomorphicPoincareSeries_zero_one` (compatibility): P(0, k, 1) = ModularForm.E k.

Unit tests:

- `holomorphicPoincare_zero_levelOne_test` (compatibility): P(0, k, 1) = ModularForm.E k for even k ≥ 4.
- `holomorphicPoincare_isCuspForm_test` (characterisation): For m ≥ 1, P(m, k, N) vanishes at every cusp of Γ₀(N).
- `holomorphicPoincare_neg_not_bounded_test` (non-example): For m ≥ 1, P(−m, k, N) is not bounded at ∞ (its expansion starts q^{−m}).
- `holomorphicPoincare_one_twelve_test` (computation): P(1, 12, 1) = c·Δ with c ≠ 0 (S_12(SL₂(ℤ)) = ℂΔ and P(1, 12, 1) ≠ 0 since its pairing with Δ is non-zero).

Acceptance checks:

- P(0, k, 1) = E_k (Mathlib's ModularForm.E); P(m, k, N) ∈ S_k(Γ₀(N)) for m ≥ 1; P(−m, k, N) ∈ M^!_k(Γ₀(N)) with principal part q^{−m} at ∞.

<a id="QM-3-maass-poincare-series"></a>

### Maass–Poincaré series Q(−m, k, N)

**Definition** (`QM.3/maass-poincare-series`). For N ≥ 1, even k ≥ 4 and m ≥ 1: Q(−m, k, N; τ) := Σ_{A ∈ Γ∞\Γ₀(N)} (ψ_m|_{2−k}A)(τ) with seed ψ_m(τ) := P(k−1, 4πmv)·e(−mτ), where P(s, x) = γ(s, x)/Γ(s) is Tau Ceti's TauCeti.regularizedGamma. The seed is Hejhal's M-Whittaker seed of Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades (6.7) in its intended normalisation: (1/(k−1)!)·M_{k/2}(−4πmv)e(−mu) with M_s(y) = |y|^{(k−2)/2}M_{(1−k/2)sgn y, s−1/2}(|y|) (DLMF 8.5.4 gives M_{(k−2)/2,(k−1)/2}(x) = (k−1)x^{1−k/2}e^{x/2}γ(k−1, x)); BOR print the weight-k normalisation, which is undefined here (sourceIssue E404). Equivalently ψ_m = e(−mτ) − Γ(k−1, 4πmv)e(−mτ)/(k−2)!, the sum of the holomorphic term q^{−m} and a decaying non-holomorphic basis function of weight 2 − k.

Hypotheses and conventions:

- k even ≥ 4, m ≥ 1, N ≥ 1; weight of Q is 2 − k ≤ −2.
- The case k = 2 (weight 0, Rademacher-type sums, needing analytic continuation) is not part of this definition.

Source support:

- [bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008](#reference-bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008), (6.7), p. 15. The definition as printed (with the weight slip E404).
- [bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008](#reference-bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008), Prop. 6.2, p. 16. Fixes the intended normalisation of the seed.
- [dlmf-incomplete-gamma](#reference-dlmf-incomplete-gamma), §8.5, eq. 8.5.4. Identifies the Whittaker seed with the regularized lower incomplete gamma function.

Direct prerequisites: [QM.3/upper-incomplete-gamma](#QM-3-upper-incomplete-gamma), [QM.3/nonholomorphic-fourier-basis-decaying](#QM-3-nonholomorphic-fourier-basis-decaying), `tauceti:TauCeti.regularizedGamma`, `tauceti:TauCeti.lowerIncompleteGamma_eq_integral`, `mathlib:CongruenceSubgroup.Gamma0`, `mathlib:EisensteinSeries.summable_norm_eisSummand`.

Construction or proof route:

1. Seed bounds: 0 ≤ P(k−1, x) ≤ min(1, x^{k−1}/(k−1)!) (γ(s, x) ≤ x^s/s), so |ψ_m(τ)| ≤ C min(e^{2πmv}, v^{k−1}e^{2πmv}).
2. For A = (a b; c d) with c ≠ 0: Im Aτ = v/|cτ + d|² ≤ 1/(c²v), so |(ψ_m|_{2−k}A)(τ)| ≤ C′v^{k−1}|cτ + d|^{−k} on compacta; the series converges absolutely and locally uniformly (k ≥ 3), with its derivatives.
3. Well defined on Γ∞\Γ₀(N): ψ_m(τ + 1) = ψ_m(τ) and weight 2 − k even.

Uses that determine the API:

- Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades Prop. 6.2, §6.2: explicit harmonic Maass forms with ξ-image P(m, k, N) and D^{k−1}-image −m^{k−1}P(−m, k, N)
- Bruinier–Funke Remark 3.10: Hejhal Poincaré series span H_k^+ for k < 0 (level one: QM.3/level-one-plus-space-spanned-by-poincare-series)
- Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades §7: the example Q(−1, 4, 9) with rational holomorphic part

Named declarations and API:

- `maassPoincareSeries` (data): Q(−m, k, N; τ) = Σ_{A ∈ Γ∞\Γ₀(N)} (ψ_m|_{2−k}A)(τ).
- `maassPoincareSeed` (data): ψ_m(τ) = P(k−1, 4πm Im τ)·e(−mτ).
- `maassPoincareSeed_eq` (characterisation): ψ_m = e(−mτ) − Γ(k−1, 4πmv)e(−mτ)/(k−2)!.
- `maassPoincareSeries_summable` (other): Absolute, locally uniform convergence with all derivatives.
- `maassPoincareSeries_toHarmonic` (constructor): Q(−m, k, N) as an element of H_{2−k}^+(Γ₀(N)) (QM.3/maass-poincare-series-harmonic).

Unit tests:

- `maassPoincare_seed_test` (computation): ψ_m(τ) = e(−mτ) − Γ(k−1, 4πmv)e(−mτ)/(k−2)! for every τ. Here m ≥ 1.
- `maassPoincare_mem_plusSpace_test` (characterisation): Q(−m, k, N) underlies an element of H_{2−k}^+(Γ₀(N)).
- `maassPoincare_constant_term_test` (computation): For N = 1, m = 1, k = 12 the holomorphic part has constant term −65520/691.
- `maassPoincare_not_weaklyHolomorphic_test` (non-example): Q(−m, k, N) is not holomorphic: ξ_{2−k}Q(−m, k, N) = (4πm)^{k−1}/(k−2)!·P(m, k, N) ≠ 0 whenever S_k(Γ₀(N)) ≠ 0 and P(m, k, N) ≠ 0 (e.g. N = 1, k = 12, m = 1).

Acceptance checks:

- The identity term of Q(−m, k, N) is q^{−m} − Γ(k−1, 4πmv)q^{−m}/(k−2)!, matching the leading terms q^{−m} of Q⁺ and −Γ(k−1, 4πmy)q^{−m}/(k−2)! of Q⁻ in BOR Prop. 6.2.
- For N = 1, m = 1, k = 12: the constant term of the holomorphic part is −65520/691 ≈ −94.8191 (BOR Prop. 6.2; numerically confirmed), and a⁺(1) ≈ −1842.89472.

<a id="QM-3-maass-poincare-series-harmonic"></a>

### Q(−m, k, N) is a harmonic Maass form in H_{2−k}^+

**Theorem** (`QM.3/maass-poincare-series-harmonic`). For N ≥ 1, even k ≥ 4, m ≥ 1: Q(−m, k, N) ∈ H_{2−k}^+(Γ₀(N)); its principal part at ∞ is q^{−m} + a constant, and at every cusp of Γ₀(N) inequivalent to ∞ its principal part is constant (Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades Prop. 6.2, first assertion).

Hypotheses and conventions:

- As in QM.3/maass-poincare-series.

Source support:

- [bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008](#reference-bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008), Prop. 6.2, p. 15. The membership (BOR's H_{2−k} = H^+_{2−k}).
- [bruinier-funke-2004](#reference-bruinier-funke-2004), Remark 3.10, p. 15. Same membership in the vector-valued setting.

Direct prerequisites: [QM.3/maass-poincare-series](#QM-3-maass-poincare-series), [QM.3/harmonic-maass-form](#QM-3-harmonic-maass-form), [QM.3/laplacian-slash-equivariance](#QM-3-laplacian-slash-equivariance), [QM.3/nonholomorphic-fourier-basis-decaying](#QM-3-nonholomorphic-fourier-basis-decaying), [QM.3/plus-space-principal-part-characterisation](#QM-3-plus-space-principal-part-characterisation).

Construction or proof route:

1. Harmonic: Δ_{2−k}ψ_m = 0 (holomorphic term plus the decaying basis function, QM.3/nonholomorphic-fourier-basis-decaying) and Δ commutes with the slash (QM.3/laplacian-slash-equivariance); the series converges with two derivatives locally uniformly.
2. Invariance: re-indexing over Γ∞\Γ₀(N); C²: locally uniform convergence of derivatives.
3. Growth at ∞: Q − ψ_m = O(v^{k−1}·v^{1−k}) = O(1) (sum over c ≠ 0 of v^{k−1}|cτ + d|^{−k} is O(v^{1−k}) times v^{k−1}), so Q − q^{−m} is bounded; at a cusp σ∞ not equivalent to ∞ no term is fixed and (Q|σ) is bounded.
4. Hence exponential growth everywhere, and after removing q^{−m} (at ∞) Q is bounded at the cusps, so by QM.3/plus-space-principal-part-characterisation (with the boundedness implying the non-holomorphic terms decay) Q ∈ H_{2−k}^+.

Acceptance checks:

- For N = 1 the principal part is q^{−m} + a⁺(0).

<a id="QM-3-xi-maass-poincare-series"></a>

### ξ_{2−k}Q(−m, k, N) = (4πm)^{k−1}/(k−2)!·P(m, k, N)

**Theorem** (`QM.3/xi-maass-poincare-series`). For N ≥ 1, even k ≥ 4, m ≥ 1: ξ_{2−k}(Q(−m, k, N)) = ((4πm)^{k−1}/(k−2)!)·P(m, k, N) (Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades §6.2).

Hypotheses and conventions:

- As in QM.3/maass-poincare-series.

Source support:

- [bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008](#reference-bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008), §6.2, p. 16. Exactly the statement (BOR derive it from (1.3) and the expansions; here it is proved termwise).

Direct prerequisites: [QM.3/maass-poincare-series](#QM-3-maass-poincare-series), [QM.3/holomorphic-poincare-series](#QM-3-holomorphic-poincare-series), [QM.3/xi-slash-equivariance](#QM-3-xi-slash-equivariance), [QM.3/nonholomorphic-fourier-basis-decaying](#QM-3-nonholomorphic-fourier-basis-decaying), [QM.3/xi-map](#QM-3-xi-map).

Construction or proof route:

1. ξ_{2−k}ψ_m = 0 − ξ_{2−k}(Γ(k−1, 4πmv)e(−mτ))/(k−2)! = (4πm)^{k−1}e(mτ)/(k−2)! (QM.3/nonholomorphic-fourier-basis-decaying with w = 2 − k, n = −m, h = 1; conjugation leaves the real constant unchanged).
2. ξ_{2−k}(ψ_m|_{2−k}A) = (ξ_{2−k}ψ_m)|_kA (QM.3/xi-slash-equivariance), and ξ commutes with the locally uniformly convergent sum (with derivatives).
3. Summing over Γ∞\Γ₀(N) gives (4πm)^{k−1}/(k−2)!·P(m, k, N).

Acceptance checks:

- Consistent with QM.3/xi-fourier-expansion: a⁻(−m) = −1/(k−2)! gives leading coefficient (4πm)^{k−1}/(k−2)!.
- BOR's display: ξ_{2−k}(Q(−m, k, N; z)) = (4π)^{k−1}m^{k−1}/(k−2)!·P(m, k, N; z).

<a id="QM-3-bessel-j-bromwich-integral"></a>

### The vertical-line integral for J_ν

**Lemma** (`QM.3/bessel-j-bromwich-integral`). For real x > 0, real c > 0 and ν ∈ ℂ with Re ν > 0: J_ν(x) = (x/2)^ν·(1/(2π))∫_{−∞}^{∞}(c + iy)^{−ν−1}exp(c + iy − x²/(4(c + iy)))dy, i.e. J_ν(x) = (x/2)^ν(1/(2πi))∫_{c−i∞}^{c+i∞}t^{−ν−1}exp(t − x²/(4t))dt, the integral converging absolutely (t^{−ν−1} the principal power). This is the vertical-line form of Schläfli's loop integral (DLMF 10.9.19) and the J-analogue of QM.2/modified-bessel-i-bromwich-integral.

Hypotheses and conventions:

- x > 0, c > 0, Re ν > 0.

Source support:

- [dlmf-chapter-10](#reference-dlmf-chapter-10), §10.9(ii), equation 10.9.19. Schläfli's loop integral; for Re ν > 0 the loop around the negative axis may be opened to the vertical line Re t = c (the integrand is O(|t|^{−Re ν−1}) there), which is the form stated.

Direct prerequisites: [QM.2/bromwich-integral-reciprocal-gamma](#QM-2-bromwich-integral-reciprocal-gamma), [QM.2/bessel-function-j](#QM-2-bessel-function-j).

Construction or proof route:

1. Expand exp(−x²/(4t)) = Σ_j (−x²/4)^j t^{−j}/j!.
2. On Re t = c: |t^{−ν−1−j}| ≤ e^{π|Im ν|/2}|t|^{−Re ν−1}c^{−j} and |e^t| = e^c, so Σ_j ∫|term|dy ≤ e^{c + π|Im ν|/2 + x²/(4c)}∫|c + iy|^{−Re ν−1}dy < ∞ (Re ν > 0); exchange sum and integral.
3. Each term: (1/(2π))∫(c + iy)^{−(ν+1+j)}e^{c+iy}dy = 1/Γ(ν + j + 1) by QM.2/bromwich-integral-reciprocal-gamma (Re(ν + 1 + j) > 1).
4. Sum: (x/2)^ν Σ_j(−1)^j(x²/4)^j/(j!Γ(ν + j + 1)) = J_ν(x) (QM.2/bessel-function-j).

Acceptance checks:

- Replacing x by ix formally turns it into QM.2/modified-bessel-i-bromwich-integral.
- ν = 1/2: both sides equal √(2/(πx))·sin x.

<a id="QM-3-holomorphic-poincare-series-fourier-expansion"></a>

### Fourier coefficients of holomorphic Poincaré series

**Theorem** (`QM.3/holomorphic-poincare-series-fourier-expansion`). For even k ≥ 4 and m, N ≥ 1: P(m, k, N) = q^m + Σ_{n≥1} a(m, k, N; n)q^n with a(m, k, N; n) = 2π(−1)^{k/2}(n/m)^{(k−1)/2} Σ_{c>0, N|c} K(m, n, c)/c · J_{k−1}(4π√(mn)/c) for n ≥ 1 (the q^m term included in the n = m term by the Kronecker delta convention of BOR (6.5)); and P(−m, k, N) = q^{−m} + Σ_{n≥1} a(−m, k, N; n)q^n with a(−m, k, N; n) = 2π(−1)^{k/2}(n/m)^{(k−1)/2}Σ_{c>0, N|c} K(−m, n, c)/c · I_{k−1}(4π√(mn)/c) (Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades Prop. 6.1).

Hypotheses and conventions:

- k even ≥ 4, m ≥ 1, N ≥ 1; J_ν = QM.2/bessel-function-j, I_ν = QM.2/modified-bessel-function-i; a(±m, k, N; n) real.

Source support:

- [bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008](#reference-bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008), Prop. 6.1, p. 15. Part 1; part 2 is the same with K(−m, n, c) and I_{k−1}. BOR give no proof ('well known (for example, see [11, 15])').
